Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Askeladden: A lanky young man of about eighteen with messy straw-blond hair, sharp blue-grey eyes, a narrow freckled face and a crooked, easy smile. He wears a faded red knitted cap, a patched undyed linen shirt, a short brown wool waistcoat with deep pockets, grey-brown knee breeches, grey wool stockings and worn leather shoes.
- the Troll: An enormous, ancient troll three times the height of a man, with grey-green skin like weathered rock patched with moss and lichen, a long knobbly nose, tiny black eyes under bushy brows, a wide mouth with two stubby teeth, huge ears, a tangled beard like dry grass and a young spruce growing from the top of his head. He wears a ragged hide tunic tied with rope and goes barefoot on huge flat feet.

Setting:
- the Grey Crag: A bare, rounded grey granite mountain rising straight out of the far shore of a wide mountain lake, with a strip of pebble beach, a few wind-bent birches and mossy boulders at its foot, and a tall, dark crack low in the rock face that leads inside.

Story world: Old rural Norway. The King's manor is a cluster of dark log buildings with turf roofs, carved gables and a hall with small leaded windows, on the shore of a wide, deep mountain lake. Straight across the lake rises the Grey Crag, where the trolls live behind a crack in the rock. The seven silver ducks are ordinary-sized ducks of solid, shining silver. The kneading trough is a long, shallow, oval trough of dark wood, big enough for a man to sit in; Askeladden rows it with a short wooden paddle. The troll's bedspread is a heavy quilt of alternating silver and gold squares. The golden harp is a small golden lap harp with a carved swan's head at the top.

This story's season, light and colours: Late summer on a wide mountain lake: cool clear mornings, silver glints on grey-blue water and low golden evening sun on bare rock. Inside the mountain: smoky orange firelight and deep brown shadow.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Characters

Askeladden askeladden · Askeladden

Den yngste sønnen som alle undervurderer, men som er arbeidsom, rolig og smart nok til å overvinne både brødrenes intriger og trollets trusler.

A lanky young man of about eighteen with messy straw-blond hair, sharp blue-grey eyes, a narrow freckled face and a crooked, easy smile. He wears a faded red knitted cap, a patched undyed linen shirt, a short brown wool waistcoat with deep pockets, grey-brown knee breeches, grey wool stockings and worn leather shoes.

Den eldste broren eldste-bror · the Eldest Brother

Stallgutten som helst vil slippe unna arbeid, og som sammen med broren skryter Askeladden inn i det ene farlige oppdraget etter det andre.

A tall, broad-shouldered man in his mid-twenties with a square jaw, short dark-brown hair, a thin moustache and a smug, lazy expression. He wears a dark-green wool jacket over a white shirt, brown breeches and tall black boots.

Den mellomste broren mellomste-bror · the Middle Brother

Gartnergutten som blir grønn av misunnelse når lillebroren får skryt, og som hvisker med stallmesteren.

A heavyset man of about twenty-two with round red cheeks, curly ginger hair, a sulky mouth and small, suspicious eyes. He wears a mustard-yellow wool tunic with a rope belt, patched brown trousers and wooden clogs.

Kongen kongen · the King

Herskeren på kongsgården som setter harde krav, men belønner Askeladden når han lykkes med de umulige oppdragene.

A stout, elderly king with a long white beard, rosy cheeks, small round spectacles on a red nose and a greedy, delighted look whenever he sees treasure. He wears a simple gold crown, a long red robe trimmed with white fur and gold embroidery, and soft red slippers.

Trollet trollet · the Troll

En farlig og grådig kjempe som bor i fjellet på andre siden av vannet og vokter sine skatter, men lar seg lure av Askeladdens svar og knep.

An enormous, ancient troll three times the height of a man, with grey-green skin like weathered rock patched with moss and lichen, a long knobbly nose, tiny black eyes under bushy brows, a wide mouth with two stubby teeth, huge ears, a tangled beard like dry grass and a young spruce growing from the top of his head. He wears a ragged hide tunic tied with rope and goes barefoot on huge flat feet.

Trolldattera trolldattera · the Troll's Daughter

Trollets datter som vokter Askeladden og til slutt blir lurt når han får henne til å låne ham kniven.

A huge troll woman, about three times as tall as a man, with a broad moss-green face, a long bumpy nose, small squinting eyes, heavy arms and one enormous reddish-brown braid that reaches the floor. She wears a patched grey wool dress, a faded red shawl and a coarse sacking apron, and goes barefoot.

#01 · askeladden, eldste-bror, mellomste-bror
simplified · after paragraph 3
De to eldste kom til kongsgården og fikk arbeid der, den ene hos stallmesteren og den andre hos hagemesteren. Askeladden gikk etter. På ryggen bar han et stort knadetrau, et trau til å elte brøddeig i. Det var det eneste foreldrene hadde etterlatt seg, og brødrene hadde ikke villet ha det. Trauet var så tungt at han gikk krumbøyd under det, men han ville ikke la det stå igjen.

Askeladden gikk etter, krumbøyd under knadetrauet.

Alt: De to eldste brødrene går inn gjennom porten til kongsgården. Langt bak dem kommer Askeladden gående, krumbøyd under et stort knadetrau av tre.

english · after paragraph 3
The two eldest came to the King’s manor and were taken on there, one under the Master of the Stables and the other under the head gardener. Ash-Lad came trudging after them with a great wooden kneading trough on his back. It was the only thing their parents had left, and his brothers hadn’t wanted it. It was heavy enough to bend him double, but he would not leave it behind.

Ash-Lad came trudging after, bent double under the kneading trough.

Alt: The two elder brothers walk through the gate of the King's manor. Far behind them, Ash-Lad trudges up the road, bent double under a big wooden kneading trough.

A dirt road winding up to the gate of the royal manor on a grey morning. Far ahead, the Eldest Brother and the Middle Brother stride through the gate without looking back. Far behind them, Askeladden trudges up the road bent double under a huge oval wooden kneading trough strapped to his back, his face set and stubborn.

Rett overfor kongsgården, på den andre siden av et vann, bodde et troll. Trollet hadde sju ender av rent sølv. De lå og duppet ute på vannet og blinket i sola, så man kunne se dem helt fra kongsgården. Kongen sto og så på dem hver eneste dag. Han hadde så lyst på de endene.

#03 · askeladden
simplified · after paragraph 13
Han fikk kornet, helte det i knadetrauet og rodde over vannet i det. På den andre siden gikk han langs strandkanten og strødde korn. Han strødde og strødde. Endene kom svømmende etter, den ene etter den andre, og til slutt klatret alle sju opp i trauet for å spise. Da skjøv Askeladden fra land og rodde tilbake så fort han kunne.

Én etter én klatret sølvendene opp i trauet for å spise.

Alt: Askeladden går langs stranden under berget og strør korn. Sju sølvender svømmer etter ham og klatrer opp i knadetrauet, som står fullt av korn i vannkanten.

english · after paragraph 13
He got his grain, tipped it into the kneading trough and rowed across the lake in it. On the far shore he walked along the water’s edge scattering grain, scattering and scattering, until the silver ducks came paddling after it one by one and climbed right into the trough to eat. Then he pushed off and rowed back as hard as he could.

One by one, the silver ducks climbed into the trough to eat.

Alt: Ash-Lad walks along the beach below the mountain scattering grain. Seven silver ducks paddle after him and climb into the kneading trough, which is full of grain at the water's edge.

- the Troll: An enormous, ancient troll three times the height of a man, with grey-green skin like weathered rock patched with moss and lichen, a long knobbly nose, tiny black eyes under bushy brows, a wide mouth with two stubby teeth, huge ears, a tangled beard like dry grass and a young spruce growing from the top of his head. Story world: A snowy spruce forest in old Norway, long ago, where the animals can talk. Below the forest lies the Frozen Lake, a small forest lake under thick, snow-dusted ice. The bear and the fox are natural wild animals without clothes: they walk on four legs, but can sit up and use their front paws like hands.

Characters

Bjørnen bjorn · the Bear

Stor og sterk, men lett å lure; prøver å lære å fiske og ender med å bli gjort til syndebukk.

A huge, heavy, slow-moving brown bear, taller than a man when he rears up, with thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose and a patient, slightly puzzled look. He has enormous flat paws with blunt claws and, unlike bears today, a long, fine, plume-like bushy tail that reaches the ground and sweeps the snow behind him.

Den stubbrumpete bjørnen bjorn-stubbrumpet · the Stub-tailed Bear

Bjørnen etter isfisket, med bare en liten halestump igjen. Han bærer ikke nag, og han stoler fortsatt på reven.

The same huge, heavy, slow-moving brown bear after his fishing trip: thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose, a patient, slightly puzzled look and enormous flat paws with blunt claws. His long tail is gone: all that is left is a tiny, round, fluffy stump on his big round bottom.

Reven rev · the Fox

En slu rev som lurer bjørnen til å fiske med halen, spiser opp julesmøret deres og får bjørnen til å ta skylden.

A slim, light-footed, long-legged red fox with sleek, bright flame-red winter fur, a snow-white chin, throat and chest, black lower legs and paws, tall pointed ears with black backs, narrow amber eyes with a sly sideways glance and a long, pointed snout with long whiskers. His big, bushy red tail ends in a clean white tip.

Then Reynard crept back to the tub. A little scrap of butter was still stuck in a crack in the wood. He picked it out with his claw, tiptoed back to the Bear and smeared it on his backside. Then he lay down again and shut his eyes, the picture of innocence.

Alt: The Bear lies asleep on his side on the sunny slope. Behind him the Fox tiptoes up and smears a little scrap of butter on the Bear's backside. The empty tub lies under the spruce bush.

A sunny, snowy slope in the forest in the afternoon, the shadows growing long and blue. The fox's stolen fish are five fat silver fish tied together by their tails with a piece of string. The butter tub is a small, round wooden tub with a flat lid and two bent-wood hoops, about as tall as the fox and full of yellow butter. The bear and the fox are natural wild animals without clothes: they walk on four legs, but can sit up and use their front paws like hands.

Askeladden askeladden · Askeladden

Den yngste prinsen som blir avvist av brødrene, men som møter Dukken i gresset og viser godhet og mot.

A tall, gangly young prince of about nineteen with long arms and legs, a long face with deep dimples when he smiles, warm hazel eyes, a straight nose and copper-red hair cut in a round bowl cut. He wears a sky-blue linen smock with a small silver clasp at the collar, belted with a broad brown leather belt, loose grey wool breeches and tall, worn brown riding boots.

Dukken i gresset dukken-i-gresset · the Tiny Grass Maiden

En bitteliten, praktfullt pyntet kvinne som kan spinne, veve og sy på en dag, og som forvandles til full størrelse etter å ha falt i vannet.

A tiny young woman of about eighteen, no taller than a man's hand, perfectly formed with the natural proportions of a grown girl, slim and light on her feet, with a small heart-shaped face, a tiny upturned nose, sparkling green eyes, rosy cheeks and a bright smile. Her straw-coloured hair hangs in two long plaits tied with grass-green ribbons, with daisies tucked in. She wears a fine ankle-length white linen dress with a grass-green sash, and a faint glow shines about her.

Dukken i gresset (stor) dukken-i-gresset-stor · the Grass Maiden

Dukken i gresset etter at havmannen har båret henne opp av vannet: like stor som et hvilket som helst voksent menneske, og mye vakrere enn før.

A young woman of about eighteen, now as tall as any grown woman, slim and graceful, with a small heart-shaped face, a tiny upturned nose, sparkling green eyes, rosy cheeks and a bright smile. Her straw-coloured hair hangs in two long plaits tied with grass-green ribbons, under a wreath of daisies and buttercups. She wears a fine ankle-length white linen dress embroidered with little green leaves along the hem and sleeves, and a grass-green sash.

Kongen kongen · the King

Faren som setter den strenge prøven for svigerdøtrene og til slutt velger Askeladden og Dukken i gresset.

A tall, thin, elderly king with narrow, sloping shoulders, a long, lined face, a long pointed nose, shrewd grey eyes under thin arched eyebrows and a neat, pointed grey goatee. He wears a tall, pointed gold crown, a long deep-blue wool robe with a wide border of rosemaling flowers embroidered in red, white and yellow, and pointed dark-blue leather shoes.

Havmannen havmannen · the Merman

Den mystiske skikkelsen som redder Dukken i gresset fra vannet og gjør at hun kommer opp forvandlet.

A big, broad-chested merman, a man from the waist up and a great salmon from the waist down, with a broad, weathered, kind face, a wide flat nose, twinkling sea-green eyes, long wet dark-green hair hanging to his waist with strands of pondweed in it, a curly dark-green beard and a small, plain crown of tarnished gold. He wears a necklace of white river shells, and his long tail is silver with small black spots and a pink sheen, ending in a broad forked fin.

En dag sa mannen: «Nå reiser jeg bort i åtte dager, og så lenge får du være her alene.» Han pekte på fire dører i gangen. «Men inn i noen av disse rommene må du ikke gå. Gjør du det, tar jeg livet av deg når jeg kommer igjen.»

«Men inn i noen av disse rommene må du ikke gå.»

Alt: Den høye mannen står i en mørk gang med en reisesekk i hånda og peker strengt på fire lukkede, mørkerøde dører. Gutten står ved siden av og nikker.

english · after paragraph 9
One day the man said, “I’m going away for eight days. You’ll be on your own here, and you’re not to go into any of these four rooms. If you do, I’ll kill you when I get back.”

“You’re not to go into any of these four rooms.”

Alt: The tall man stands in a dark hallway with a travelling bag in his hand, pointing sternly at four closed dark-red doors. The boy stands beside him, nodding.

In the Long Hallway, lit by a single candle, the Stranger stands dressed for a journey, a leather travelling bag in one huge hand, and points a long, bony finger at the four closed oxblood-red doors, his face hard and his small black eyes glinting. The Widow's Son stands beside him with his hands behind his back, looking at the doors and nodding solemnly.

Full prompt
Reference images:
- Image 1: model sheet for the Stranger, the same character seen from three sides. Keep the Stranger's face, hair, body shape, age, colours and clothes exactly as shown. Draw the Stranger only once, in the pose this picture needs, and ignore the sheet's layout and plain background.
- Image 2: model sheet for the Widow's Son, the same character seen from three sides. Keep the Widow's Son's face, hair, body shape, age, colours and clothes exactly as shown. Draw the Widow's Son only once, in the pose this picture needs, and ignore the sheet's layout and plain background.
- Image 3: setting reference for the Long Hallway. Keep its landforms, buildings, colours and key details, and choose the viewpoint and framing this picture needs.

Create one new illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: In the Long Hallway, lit by a single candle, the Stranger stands dressed for a journey, a leather travelling bag in one huge hand, and points a long, bony finger at the four closed oxblood-red doors, his face hard and his small black eyes glinting. The Widow's Son stands beside him with his hands behind his back, looking at the doors and nodding solemnly.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Stranger: An unusually tall, gaunt figure who almost passes for a man: a long, craggy face with a stony grey complexion, a huge knobbly nose, small glinting black eyes under bushy iron-grey eyebrows, a wide, thin-lipped mouth, big pointed ears and a short, bristly iron-grey beard. He has very long arms, huge knobbly hands and enormous flat feet in big black boots, and wears a long black wool coat that reaches his ankles, buttoned with large horn buttons, and a tall, battered black hat.
- the Widow's Son: A slim, kind-faced young man of about nineteen with milk-pale skin and bright red cheeks, an oval face, a neat, narrow nose, big dark-brown eyes under thick level black eyebrows and short, glossy blue-black hair, wavy on top, with a stubborn cowlick sticking up at the crown. He wears a faded cornflower-blue sleeveless jerkin with three wooden toggles over a coarse oatmeal smock, a small red neckerchief, mended charcoal homespun trousers tied at the ankle and scuffed brown ankle boots.

Setting:
- the Long Hallway: The long, dim hallway inside a tall old house of smoke-blackened logs: rough log walls, a worn plank floor and low, heavy ceiling beams. Along one wall stand four identical closed plank doors in a row, painted dark oxblood red, each with a black iron ring handle. An iron candle holder hangs on the wall, and a small window of greenish glass sits at the far end.

Story world: Old rural Norway. The widow's son walks from a poor valley into endless spruce forest, where the Stranger's house stands alone: tall and gloomy, of smoke-blackened logs, with four forbidden rooms off its long hallway. On a shelf above the door of the first lies a whip of thorny wild-rose briar; in the second, a round grey stone as big as a loaf and a small brown clay water jug with a cork; in the third, a trapdoor over a huge round copper cauldron that boils with no fire under it; in the fourth, the black horse's plank stall. The ointment is kept in a small round blue clay jar. Near the royal manor, a great hollow linden stands alone in a green forest glade, and below the manor lies a wide brown bog. The royal handkerchief is fine white linen with a small gold crown embroidered in one corner.

This story's season, light and colours: High summer: long, bright days, green meadows and wild roses in bloom, and blue-green shade under the spruces. Inside the Stranger's house: dim candlelight, smoke-dark timber and the warm glow of copper. The bog is rust-red and olive under tall white clouds, and the battle days end in dusty golden evening light. Accents: wild-rose pink, rust orange and gleaming copper.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

#04 · enkesonnen
simplified · after paragraph 19
Det gikk akkurat som forrige gang, bare at nå holdt gutten seg i åtte dager. I det andre rommet var det heller ikke noe annet enn en hylle over døra. På den lå en kampestein, og ved siden av sto en vannkrukke.

Han rykket hånda til seg og stirret. Fingeren skinte. Den var forgylt over det hele. Han gned og gned, han skrapte og vasket, men gullet satt der det satt. Til slutt bandt han en fille rundt fingeren.

english · after paragraph 25

When he pulled it out again, it was gilded all over.

Alt: The boy kneels at an open trapdoor in the floor. Below, a great copper cauldron boils with no fire under it, and the boy stares at his finger, which gleams with gold.

In a bare, dim room, the Widow's Son kneels at the edge of an open trapdoor in the plank floor, its heavy lid propped up. Below, in a small stone cellar, a huge round copper cauldron bubbles and steams with no fire beneath it. He holds up his hand in front of his astonished face: the finger he has just dipped in is gilded all over and gleams in the gloom. Wisps of steam curl up around him.

Story world: Old rural Norway. The widow's son walks from a poor valley into endless spruce forest, where the Stranger's house stands alone: tall and gloomy, of smoke-blackened logs, with four forbidden rooms off its long hallway. On a shelf above the door of the first lies a whip of thorny wild-rose briar; in the second, a round grey stone as big as a loaf and a small brown clay water jug with a cork; in the third, a trapdoor over a huge round copper cauldron that boils with no fire under it; in the fourth, the black horse's plank stall. The ointment is kept in a small round blue clay jar. Near the royal manor, a great hollow linden stands alone in a green forest glade, and below the manor lies a wide brown bog. The royal handkerchief is fine white linen with a small gold crown embroidered in one corner.

Inside the Stranger's house: dim candlelight, smoke-dark timber and the warm glow of copper. The bog is rust-red and olive under tall white clouds, and the battle days end in dusty golden evening light. Accents: wild-rose pink, rust orange and gleaming copper.

The suitor carries a small, square brown leather travel bag with a brass clasp.

Den yngste kongssønnen den-yngste-kongssonnen · the Youngest Prince

Den modigste av brødrene, som holder seg våken når andre sover, finner sannheten og våger seg inn i slottet for å redde prinsessene.

A slim, brave prince in his twenties with a kind, open face, a fine straight nose, calm green-grey eyes, a quick smile and wavy dark-brown hair falling to his shoulders. He wears a forest-green hunting coat with brass buttons and a high collar, a narrow gold belt, dark-grey riding trousers tucked into tall tan boots, and a small gold brooch shaped like a ship pinned to his collar.

Sjømannen sjomannen · the Sailor

Den yngste kongssønnen i forkledning, i en stor matroskofte. Han later som han er en stakkars matros som har forlist, og siden kommer han som kremmer.

A slim young man in his twenties disguised as a poor sailor, with a kind face, a straight nose, steady green-grey eyes and a few days' dark stubble, his wavy dark-brown hair tucked under a red kerchief knotted round his head. He wears a huge, baggy, dark-blue knitted sailor's coat with wooden buttons that hangs down to his knees, patched canvas trousers and scuffed, salt-stained boots.

Den yngste prinsessa den-yngste-prinsessa · the Youngest Princess

Prinsessa som sørger i stillhet og beskytter seg med et blankt sverd, og som til slutt tør å si hvem som virkelig reddet dem.

A small, slight princess of about twenty with a round, solemn face, a short nose, deep-blue eyes under thick, level brows and a small, determined mouth. Her honey-brown hair is braided into a crown around her head. She wears a long ivory gown stitched with gold at the bodice and hem, with tight long sleeves and a narrow gold girdle, and a little silver anchor pinned at her collar.

Fugl Dam fugl-dam · the Giant Bird

En enorm fugl som spiser fire tønner rug til frokost og flyr kongssønnen og gullkronene over havet til trollprinsen.

An enormous, friendly bird as tall as a three-storey house, so big that a man reaches only to its ankle, shaped a little like a giant gull. It has a pale silver-grey back, broad silver-grey wings with black tips, a snowy-white head and breast, kind dark eyes, a big hooked golden-yellow beak and huge orange webbed feet. From the back of its neck rises one enormous, stiff, copper-red feather, as thick as a young spruce.

Ridder Rød ridder-rod · Sir Red

Styrmann og rival som blir misunnelig, sviker den yngste prinsen og prøver å ta æren for redningen for å få den yngste prinsessa.

A tall, barrel-chested, vain man of about forty with a big square jaw, a cleft chin, a short straight nose held high, small, cold pale-blue eyes and a proud smirk. He has short flame-red hair and a short, pointed flame-red beard. He wears a round, polished steel helmet with a stiff red crest, a long scarlet surcoat with a gold border over a shirt of chainmail, a wide black belt with a big gold buckle and tall black boots.

Trollkongen med tolv hoder trollkongen · the Troll King

Stortrollet med tolv hoder, som sitter pyntet i en flott sal mens de tolv prinsessene plukker lus av ham, til den yngste kongssønnen hogger hodene av.

A huge, hulking troll about three times as tall as a man, with rust-red, warty skin, a broad, sagging barrel of a body, very long arms that hang down to the floor and short bowed legs. On his thick neck sits a bunch of exactly twelve small heads, packed tightly together like a bunch of turnips, each with a knobbly nose, droopy ears and a wispy tuft of pale straw-coloured hair. He wears a moth-eaten dark-blue velvet cloak with a tattered fur collar and heavy gold chains.

Trollprinsen trollprinsen · the Troll Prince

Et stort og stygt troll på øya, som gir kongssønnen sverdet og flaska, og som blir konge når trollkongen er borte.

A huge, strange troll about three times as tall as a man, shaped like a giant sack of flour, with sloping shoulders, a small head, a big soft belly, short legs and huge webbed feet like a duck's. His skin is a weathered, ruddy tan. He has a nose as long as a cucumber, small kind amber eyes, big ears like cabbage leaves and a stiff crest of dark-brown hair standing straight up like a brush. He wears a mulberry-purple velvet tunic with a wide gold belt.

Trollprinsessa trolldattera · the Troll's Daughter

Trollprinsens datter. Først er hun en liten hund som bjeffer og piper på en øy, så en vakker prinsesse. I mange år syr hun klær og lintøy til kongssønnen.

A willowy young woman of about twenty with pale, milky skin, a long, narrow face, a tiny pointed nose, big silvery-grey eyes and long, pale-blonde hair that floats and drifts around her as if she were under water. A thin, misty veil floats around her too, as if lifted by a breeze. She wears a long, flowing apricot-coloured dress with a silver belt and goes barefoot.

Kongen kongen · the King

Kongen med de tolv døtrene, som er så glad i dem at han helst vil ha dem hos seg hele tiden.

A small, wiry, elderly king with a narrow, kind, crinkly face, a small sharp nose, twinkling blue eyes, wisps of silver hair and a long silver-grey beard braided into two plaits tied with little gold rings. He wears a low, wide gold crown set with green stones, a long turquoise robe with a collar of spotted grey sealskin and silver clasps shaped like fish, and soft grey felt slippers.

Den nysgjerrige kjerringa den-nysgjerrige-kjerringa · the Nosy Old Woman

Ei gammel kjerring i ei falleferdig hytte, som spør og graver og løper rett til de andre sladrekjerringene med nyheten.

A short, bustling old woman with a plump little body on thin legs, like a robin, and a long neck that she cranes forward to see everything. She has a sharp little chin, a beaky nose, big curious eyes magnified by thick, round spectacles and wispy white hair scraped into a tiny topknot like an onion. She wears a faded lavender dress, an orange knitted shawl and a patched brown apron with a deep pocket.

Da han var på siden av skipet, løftet han på klubba igjen. Da brøt det løs en storm så det sto hvitt skum rundt skipet. english · after paragraph 50
He had hardly sat down in the boat and said “Boat, go forward!” before off it went. When he saw the ship straight ahead, he lifted the club, and they got such a fair wind that they forgot to look out for him. When he came alongside, he lifted it again, and such a storm blew up that the white foam stood round the ship and the waves came crashing over the deck, and they had better things to do than stare at him. And when he was past them, he lifted the club a third time, and then they had so much to do that nobody had a moment to wonder who he might be. Each time, he laid the club down as gently as an egg.

Such a storm blew up that the white foam stood round the ship.

Alt: The prince races past in a small iron boat, gently laying down the iron club. Beside him the ship heels over in the storm, and everyone aboard is far too busy to notice him.

On a rough, stormy sea, the small dark iron boat races along by itself with no oars and no sail, and the Youngest Prince carefully lowers the heavy iron club back into it with both hands, as gently as an egg. Close beside him the Ship heels over in a sudden gale, its sail bulging, white foam standing all round its hull and waves breaking over the deck, while tiny figures aboard haul on ropes, far too busy to look his way.

english · after paragraph 55
That evening he carried his things in, and no sooner were they inside than the old woman, who loved nothing better than a bit of news to run about with, began to ask questions. Who was he? Where was he from? Where had he been, and where was he going? What had he got in all those bundles? What was his business? And had he heard anything of the twelve princesses who had vanished all those years ago? And a great deal more besides, enough to fill a long evening. But he said he was so knocked about, and his head ached so badly from all that dreadful weather, that he couldn’t make sense of anything. She must let him rest for a few days, until he had got over all that hard work, and then she should hear everything she wanted to know, and more.

Who was he? Where was he from? Where had he been, and where was he going?

Inside, twelve small golden crowns sit side by side, shining so brightly that golden light fills the hall. The Youngest Princess steps forward with tears in her eyes and points straight at the Sailor. Her eleven sisters crowd round the cupboard, the King leans forward from his tall chair in amazement, and Sir Red stands stiff and pale.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Sailor: A slim young man in his twenties disguised as a poor sailor, with a kind face, a straight nose, steady green-grey eyes and a few days' dark stubble, his wavy dark-brown hair tucked under a red kerchief knotted round his head. He wears a huge, baggy, dark-blue knitted sailor's coat with wooden buttons that hangs down to his knees, patched canvas trousers and scuffed, salt-stained boots.
- the Youngest Princess: A small, slight princess of about twenty with a round, solemn face, a short nose, deep-blue eyes under thick, level brows and a small, determined mouth. Her honey-brown hair is braided into a crown around her head. She wears a long ivory gown stitched with gold at the bodice and hem, with tight long sleeves and a narrow gold girdle, and a little silver anchor pinned at her collar.
- the King: A small, wiry, elderly king with a narrow, kind, crinkly face, a small sharp nose, twinkling blue eyes, wisps of silver hair and a long silver-grey beard braided into two plaits tied with little gold rings. He wears a low, wide gold crown set with green stones, a long turquoise robe with a collar of spotted grey sealskin and silver clasps shaped like fish, and soft grey felt slippers.
- Sir Red: A tall, barrel-chested, vain man of about forty with a big square jaw, a cleft chin, a short straight nose held high, small, cold pale-blue eyes and a proud smirk. He has short flame-red hair and a short, pointed flame-red beard. He wears a round, polished steel helmet with a stiff red crest, a long scarlet surcoat with a gold border over a shirt of chainmail, a wide black belt with a big gold buckle and tall black boots.

Setting:
- the Great Hall: The great hall of the royal manor by the sea: a long, high log hall with a steep, dark-beamed roof, walls hung with red and blue woven tapestries, small-paned windows looking out over the sea, a long carved table with benches, a big stone fireplace, and at the far end, on a low platform, a tall carved royal chair and a long cushioned bench.

Story world: Old Norway by the sea, over fourteen years of voyages. The princesses' father rules a royal manor of big log halls above a sandy beach. The twelve princes sail in one big, round-bellied wooden ship. On a small rocky island stands the troll prince's castle, with a tall hall of pale stone columns; far across the sea, the Black Castle on a rocky shore holds the Troll King's gilded chamber. The little dog on the island is fluffy and white, with floppy brown ears. The old sword is long and rusty, with a plain iron hilt; the troll's bottle is round, of dark-green glass. The crown cupboard is waist-high, painted blue with red-and-white rosemaling, and holds twelve small golden crowns. The iron boat is small and dark, with no oars or sail. The eleven older princes wear matching grey-blue coats; the eleven older princesses wear long dresses in soft colours.

This story's season, light and colours: The open northern sea in all its moods, from howling gales to glassy calm: jade-green and pewter-grey waves with white foam, towering silver-grey clouds, pale luminous summer nights and clear rosy dawns. Indoors, warm lamplight and the rich glow of gold. Accents: Sir Red's scarlet, the prince's forest green and gleaming golden crowns.

Giske giske · 11/11 pictures

Giske tror hun er fanden selv, og hun vil så gjerne hjelpe til.

A forest path at night under a big, pale moon, with dark spruces on both sides. Giske strides ahead on her long black legs, grinning, pointing eagerly towards a dark farm far off between the trees and clearly about to say something loud. Picture: A forest path at night under a big, pale moon, with dark spruces on both sides. Giske strides ahead on her long black legs, grinning, pointing eagerly towards a dark farm far off between the trees and clearly about to say something loud. Close behind her creep the Skinny Thief, clutching his empty sack, and the Plump Thief, with his coil of rope, both pressing a finger to their lips and glancing around in panic.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Giske: A very tall, strong housekeeper of about thirty, a head taller than any man, with extremely long legs and big bare feet. She has a long oval face, a wide eager smile, a small turned-up nose, bright hazel eyes and flaxen hair wound into a tall bun. Her plum-purple homespun dress is hacked off raggedly at the knees, and her arms and legs are smeared greasy black with tallow and soot like a chimney sweep's, with sooty smudges on her face. A ring of iron keys hangs at her belt.
- the Skinny Thief: A skinny, jittery thief of about thirty, a head shorter than Giske, with a long pale face, a long pointy nose, big frightened eyes, a wispy ginger goatee and lank hair under a floppy black knitted stocking cap. He wears a patched charcoal wool jacket too short in the arms, grey striped breeches, grey stockings and shoes wrapped in rags, and carries an empty sack under his arm.
- the Plump Thief: A short, round, nervous thief of about forty, much shorter than Giske, with a round red face, puffy cheeks, a stubbly double chin, tiny eyes, a big bushy black moustache and a bald head under a greasy brown wool cap. He wears a tight mustard-brown waistcoat with one button missing over a grey shirt, baggy brown trousers held up with a rope and big clumsy boots, and carries a coil of rope over his shoulder.

Story world: Old rural Norway, in a scattered farming parish of grey log farms with turf roofs among fields, spruce forest and bogs. The widower's small farm has a low log house with a stone chimney and a field of tall, ripe hemp below it. Beyond the farms lies a great, dark spruce forest. The farms that Giske and the thieves raid have a sheep shed built wall to wall with the farmer's sleeping room, a goose house of grey logs and, at the rich farmer's at the forest edge, a stabbur: a dark timber storehouse on posts with a steep little stair, hung inside with hams and sausages above shelves of round pea bread. The turnip patch is a clearing in the woods on a slope, with old stumps and rows of purple turnips, above a soft brown bog of tussocks and stumps.

This story's season, light and colours: August, between haymaking and harvest: a hot, hazy afternoon over the green-gold hemp; then three moonlit nights in deep indigo and blue-black, with a thin sickle moon, cold starlight and the small yellow glow of a lantern or candle; and a pearl-grey Sunday dawn with low mist over the brown bog and dew on purple turnips. Accents: greasy soot black, plum purple and turnip violet.

Characters

Giske giske · Giske

Husholderska som blir smurt inn med talg og sot, tror hun er fanden, og blir både ivrig hjelper og katastrofe for to tyver på nattetokt.

A very tall, strong housekeeper of about thirty, a head taller than any man, with extremely long legs and big bare feet. She has a long oval face, a wide eager smile, a small turned-up nose, bright hazel eyes and flaxen hair wound into a tall bun. Her plum-purple homespun dress is hacked off raggedly at the knees, and her arms and legs are smeared greasy black with tallow and soot like a chimney sweep's, with sooty smudges on her face. A ring of iron keys hangs at her belt.

Enkemannen enkemannen · the Widower

Mannen hun arbeider hos, som vil bli kvitt Giske og lager spøken som får henne til å tro hun er fanden.

A skinny, stooped widower of about fifty with a long, narrow, tired face, heavy-lidded eyes, a long crooked nose, hollow cheeks, a scruffy salt-and-pepper chin beard and thin dark hair combed flat. He wears a collarless undyed linen shirt, dark-blue braces, baggy grey homespun breeches, a darned heather-brown knitted wool jacket and worn wooden-soled shoes, and always has a short, curved pipe in the corner of his mouth.

Den tynne tyven tyven-tynn · the Skinny Thief

Den ene av de to sultne tyvene som tar Giske med på nattetokt fordi hun er så godt kjent på gårdene. Han er tynn og skvetten og hysjer mest av alle.

A skinny, jittery thief of about thirty, a head shorter than Giske, with a long pale face, a long pointy nose, big frightened eyes, a wispy ginger goatee and lank hair under a floppy black knitted stocking cap. He wears a patched charcoal wool jacket too short in the arms, grey striped breeches, grey stockings and shoes wrapped in rags, and carries an empty sack under his arm.

Den tykke tyven tyven-tykk · the Plump Thief

Den andre av de to tyvene. Han er liten og rund, sulten som en ulv og livredd for å bli tatt.

A short, round, nervous thief of about forty, much shorter than Giske, with a round red face, puffy cheeks, a stubbly double chin, tiny eyes, a big bushy black moustache and a bald head under a greasy brown wool cap. He wears a tight mustard-brown waistcoat with one button missing over a grey shirt, baggy brown trousers held up with a rope and big clumsy boots, and carries a coil of rope over his shoulder.

Bonden bonden · the Sheep Farmer

Bonden som våkner av skrålet i sauehuset, blir slått over ende av noe stort og svart, og setter seg til å lese og be.

A lean, wiry farmer of about forty-five with a bony, hollow-cheeked face, a hooked nose, bristly grey stubble, startled round eyes and wild, tousled grey hair, just woken from sleep. He wears only a long, loose, undyed linen nightshirt that reaches his knees, with bare skinny legs and bare feet, and holds up a small tin lantern with a candle burning inside.

Bonden med nepebråten nepebonden · the Turnip Farmer

En av de rikeste bøndene i bygda. Han ser fanden i nepeåkeren sin, lokker presten ut med en feit kalvestek og bærer ham over myra på ryggen.

A short, sturdy, bow-legged farmer of about fifty, one of the richest in the parish, with a square, weather-beaten face, a big bristly chestnut moustache, round startled eyes, bushy eyebrows and wiry grey hair sticking up under a wide, frayed straw hat. He wears a rust-orange wool waistcoat with silver buttons over a white linen shirt, green knee breeches pulled on in a hurry, long grey stockings and wooden clogs.

Presten presten · the Priest

Blir hentet for å «binde fanden», men ender hjelpeløs da bonden flykter i panikk.

A very round, heavy priest of about sixty-five with a big belly, short legs, a pink, jowly, clean-shaven face, puffy sleepy eyes, bushy white eyebrows and a fringe of white curls under a long red-and-white striped nightcap with a tassel. He wears a crumpled white nightshirt stuffed into black trousers he has dragged on in a hurry, with the braces dangling, and a pair of blue felt slippers.

At the edge of a field of tall, ripe hemp on a hazy afternoon, Giske lies fast asleep on her back among bundles of pulled hemp, snoring with her mouth open and her long legs stretched out. The Widower kneels beside her, pipe between his teeth and a small pot of greasy black soot in one hand, smearing the last streaks onto her arm with a grim, weary face. A big pair of iron shears and a long cut-off strip of plum-purple skirt lie in the stubble beside them.

Create one new illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: Night outside a grey log goose house. Out of its open door burst nine white geese, all shrieking at once with their necks stretched out and their wings flapping. The Skinny Thief and the Plump Thief are already bolting across the yard, and Giske leaps after them on her long bare black legs, her hacked-off skirt flying above her knees. In the doorway of the farmhouse, a stout, bald farmer in a white nightshirt holds up a candle and stares at her, frozen with terror.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Giske: A very tall, strong housekeeper of about thirty, a head taller than any man, with extremely long legs and big bare feet. She has a long oval face, a wide eager smile, a small turned-up nose, bright hazel eyes and flaxen hair wound into a tall bun. Her plum-purple homespun dress is hacked off raggedly at the knees, and her arms and legs are smeared greasy black with tallow and soot like a chimney sweep's, with sooty smudges on her face. A ring of iron keys hangs at her belt.
- the Skinny Thief: A skinny, jittery thief of about thirty, a head shorter than Giske, with a long pale face, a long pointy nose, big frightened eyes, a wispy ginger goatee and lank hair under a floppy black knitted stocking cap. He wears a patched charcoal wool jacket too short in the arms, grey striped breeches, grey stockings and shoes wrapped in rags, and carries an empty sack under his arm.
- the Plump Thief: A short, round, nervous thief of about forty, much shorter than Giske, with a round red face, puffy cheeks, a stubbly double chin, tiny eyes, a big bushy black moustache and a bald head under a greasy brown wool cap. He wears a tight mustard-brown waistcoat with one button missing over a grey shirt, baggy brown trousers held up with a rope and big clumsy boots, and carries a coil of rope over his shoulder.

Story world: Old rural Norway, in a scattered farming parish of grey log farms with turf roofs among fields, spruce forest and bogs. The widower's small farm has a low log house with a stone chimney and a field of tall, ripe hemp below it. Beyond the farms lies a great, dark spruce forest. The farms that Giske and the thieves raid have a sheep shed built wall to wall with the farmer's sleeping room, a goose house of grey logs and, at the rich farmer's at the forest edge, a stabbur: a dark timber storehouse on posts with a steep little stair, hung inside with hams and sausages above shelves of round pea bread. The turnip patch is a clearing in the woods on a slope, with old stumps and rows of purple turnips, above a soft brown bog of tussocks and stumps.

In the middle of the bog, the Priest sits stuck up to his waist in brown mud among the tussocks, his nightcap askew, open-mouthed with outrage. The Turnip Farmer runs off across the tussocks for his life, straw hat flying. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Priest: A very round, heavy priest of about sixty-five with a big belly, short legs, a pink, jowly, clean-shaven face, puffy sleepy eyes, bushy white eyebrows and a fringe of white curls under a long red-and-white striped nightcap with a tassel. He wears a crumpled white nightshirt stuffed into black trousers he has dragged on in a hurry, with the braces dangling, and a pair of blue felt slippers.
- the Turnip Farmer: A short, sturdy, bow-legged farmer of about fifty, one of the richest in the parish, with a square, weather-beaten face, a big bristly chestnut moustache, round startled eyes, bushy eyebrows and wiry grey hair sticking up under a wide, frayed straw hat. He wears a rust-orange wool waistcoat with silver buttons over a white linen shirt, green knee breeches pulled on in a hurry, long grey stockings and wooden clogs.
- Giske: A very tall, strong housekeeper of about thirty, a head taller than any man, with extremely long legs and big bare feet. She has a long oval face, a wide eager smile, a small turned-up nose, bright hazel eyes and flaxen hair wound into a tall bun. Her plum-purple homespun dress is hacked off raggedly at the knees, and her arms and legs are smeared greasy black with tallow and soot like a chimney sweep's, with sooty smudges on her face. A ring of iron keys hangs at her belt.

Story world: Old rural Norway, in a scattered farming parish of grey log farms with turf roofs among fields, spruce forest and bogs. The widower's small farm has a low log house with a stone chimney and a field of tall, ripe hemp below it. Beyond the farms lies a great, dark spruce forest. The farms that Giske and the thieves raid have a sheep shed built wall to wall with the farmer's sleeping room, a goose house of grey logs and, at the rich farmer's at the forest edge, a stabbur: a dark timber storehouse on posts with a steep little stair, hung inside with hams and sausages above shelves of round pea bread. The turnip patch is a clearing in the woods on a slope, with old stumps and rows of purple turnips, above a soft brown bog of tussocks and stumps.

This story's season, light and colours: August, between haymaking and harvest: a hot, hazy afternoon over the green-gold hemp; then three moonlit nights in deep indigo and blue-black, with a thin sickle moon, cold starlight and the small yellow glow of a lantern or candle; and a pearl-grey Sunday dawn with low mist over the brown bog and dew on purple turnips. Accents: greasy soot black, plum purple and turnip violet.

Gjertrud's home is a small, low log cottage with a mossy turf roof and a squat grey stone chimney, alone at the edge of a spruce forest. Inside is one smoky, firelit room: an open stone hearth with a smoke hood and chimney above it, a big, round, flat iron griddle over the embers, a long wooden baking board dusted with flour, a rolling pin and a wooden bench by the door. The flatbreads are lefser: big, thin and round, pale with brown speckles. Every one Gjertrud rolls, however tiny the scrap of dough, spreads on the griddle until it covers it from rim to rim.

Characters

Gjertrud gjertrud · Gjertrud

En kvinne som baker lefser, men er så gjerrig at hun ikke vil dele, selv når hun blir bedt pent.

A stout, square-built farm woman of about fifty-five with a square jaw, pinched thin lips, a sharp little upturned nose, small darting black eyes and two thick iron-grey plaits hanging over her shoulders. On her head sits a tall, pointed, bright-scarlet knitted stocking cap with a tassel at the tip. She wears a black wool bodice over a white linen blouse with rolled-up sleeves, a long charcoal-grey homespun skirt and a flour-dusted white apron.

Vår Herre varherre · Our Lord

En vandrer som ber om mat, og som straffer Gjertrud når hun nekter å gi fra seg noe.

A very old, tall and slightly stooped wanderer with a long, gentle face, deep-set, kind blue-grey eyes, a high wrinkled forehead, thin snow-white hair to his shoulders and a long, flowing white beard that reaches his belt. He wears a plain, ankle-length hooded robe of brown homespun tied with a rope and simple sandals over woollen foot-wraps, and leans on a tall, knobbly wooden staff. A humble traveller with no halo.

St. Peter sankt-peder · St Peter

Følgesvennen som vandrer sammen med Vår Herre og deler sulten og reisen.

A short, sturdy, round-shouldered old man of about sixty-five with a round, cheerful face, a shiny bald head with a fringe of short grey hair around the back, big ears, a broad flat nose, bright brown eyes and a short, bristly grey beard. He wears a knee-length faded green tunic with a leather belt, brown woollen leggings, a short brown hooded cape and worn leather boots, with a small bronze key hanging from his belt. No halo.

- the Neighbour: A nosy, pot-bellied farmer of about fifty with a round, clean-shaven face, a long, pointed, twitchy nose, narrow doubtful eyes with one eyebrow always raised, big pink ears that stick straight out and short, spiky ginger hair. A birch and a rowan tree heavy with red berries stand in the yard, and a narrow path zigzags steeply down towards the valley and a small town far below.

Gudbrand's small farm lies high up on a steep hillside, and a narrow path zigzags down past the neighbour's farm to the valley road and a small market town far below. Inside the cottage is one warm room with a fireplace, a long table with benches, a painted cupboard and a big wooden chest. Gudbrand and his wife have three children: a boy of about twelve with short black hair and a green jumper, a girl of about nine with two stubby fair plaits and a red dress, and a small boy of about six in a long white shirt. The animals: a black cow with a white face, a sandy-yellow fjord horse with a striped pale mane, a fat pink pig, a white nanny goat, a woolly white sheep, a big white goose and a cinnamon-brown rooster.

Accents: the wife’s cornflower-blue apron and rowan red.

On the road between them lies the inn, a big, low log house with a lantern at the door and a goat shed behind. The meal is carried in a grey sack. The magic cloth is a square white linen tablecloth with a red woven zigzag border, and the swapped one looks exactly the same. The stick is a knobbly old stick of pale birch wood, about as long as the boy is tall.

En gammel, fattig og skrøpelig kvinne som tviler på mirakler, men som trenger hjelpen gutten prøver å skaffe.

A thin, frail old woman of about sixty-five, a little stooped, with a long, gentle, deeply lined face, tired grey eyes, a thin mouth and one eyebrow often raised in doubt. Her grey hair hangs in one thin braid over her shoulder. She wears a faded plum-coloured homespun dress, a darned brown knitted shawl, a long patched linen apron and wooden clogs.

Nordavinden nordavinden · the North Wind

En kraftfull og lunefull vind som først tar, men som også gir magiske gaver som erstatning.

A huge, grumbling old man made of swirling white and pale-grey cloud, with no legs, only a long, whirling tail of mist and snowflakes. He has a broad, weathered face with puffed-out round cheeks, icy-blue eyes, great bushy white eyebrows, a thick moustache like drifted snow and a long, frosty white beard that streams away in the wind, and big, soft hands of cloud. Snowflakes and tiny icicles glitter in his tangled white hair.

Gjestgiveren gjestgiveren · the Innkeeper

En lur krovert som stjeler de magiske gavene, men blir stoppet når gutten gjennomskuer ham.

A tall, gangly innkeeper of about fifty with a long, narrow face, a much too wide, toothy smile, small glittering eyes, a long pointed chin and oily black hair twisted into one big curl on his forehead. He wears a wine-red waistcoat with shiny brass buttons over a white linen shirt with rolled sleeves, a long blue-and-white striped apron, dark breeches and a wide black leather money belt that jingles with coins.

Bukken bukken · the Billy Goat

En magisk bukk som kan lage gullpenger når gutten sier de riktige ordene.

A small, sturdy billy goat about the size of a large dog, with a shaggy snow-white coat, a light-grey face with a little pointed grey beard, bright amber eyes with slot-shaped pupils, short, curved, ridged horns, a stubby tail and neat black hooves. Around his neck he wears a red leather collar hung with two small brass bells.

- the Billy Goat: A small, sturdy billy goat about the size of a large dog, with a shaggy snow-white coat, a light-grey face with a little pointed grey beard, bright amber eyes with slot-shaped pupils, short, curved, ridged horns, a stubby tail and neat black hooves. Around his neck he wears a red leather collar hung with two small brass bells.

Create the cover illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: The dewy meadow of the Hill Farm just before sunrise. The Cow stands side-on by the split-rail fence, calmly chewing, while along the top rail beside her perch the Rooster, the Cuckoo and the Black Grouse in a row, each one puffed up and gazing at her possessively, as if she belonged to him alone. The Cow rolls one patient eye towards them. Pale rose light glows over the spruce ridge behind.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Cow: A gentle, sturdy old Norwegian farm cow with a glossy reddish-brown coat, a broad white stripe running along her back and down her tail, a white belly, white-speckled legs, a pink nose, big, calm brown eyes with long dark lashes and two short, pale, upward-curving horns. A small brass bell hangs from a leather strap around her neck. She chews her cud slowly and never hurries.
- the Rooster: A sleek, swaggering farmyard rooster with jet-black plumage that shimmers beetle-green in the light, a tall, jagged scarlet comb standing straight up, long dangling scarlet wattles, small white earlobes, fiery orange eyes, a sharp slate-grey beak, slate-grey legs with long spurs, and a fountain of long, curving green-black sickle feathers for a tail. He holds his head high and his chest puffed out.
- the Cuckoo: A slim, sleek common cuckoo, much smaller than the rooster, with a smooth ash-blue-grey head, back and wings, a white belly finely barred with thin dark stripes, a long, rounded dark-grey tail edged with little white spots, bright yellow rings around his round, sleepy eyes, a short, slightly curved dark beak with a yellow base and small yellow feet. One tuft of feathers always sticks up at the back of his head.
- the Black Grouse: A large, calm black grouse cock, a little bigger than the rooster, with glossy blue-black plumage, a bright-red fleshy arch like an eyebrow above each eye, a white bar across each wing, a fluffy snow-white puff of feathers under his tail, and a lyre-shaped tail whose two outer feathers curl outwards like hooks. He has feathered grey legs, a short black beak and wise, kind dark eyes, and stands tall and dignified like a judge.

Setting:
- the Hill Farm: A small, poor hill farm at the edge of a birch-and-spruce wood: a low grey log cowshed with a turf roof and a small hatch high in its wall, a grey split-rail fence of slanting poles along a dewy meadow, a tall white birch whose lowest branch reaches out over the fence, and a slope of heather and bog rising behind towards a bare moor and a dark spruce ridge.

Story world: Old rural Norway, where the birds of farm, forest and moor can talk. The Rooster, the Cuckoo and the Black Grouse have bought one cow together and agreed that whoever wakes first in the morning shall have her. She grazes the meadow of a small hill farm at the edge of a birch-and-spruce wood. The Rooster lives in the hen loft of the cowshed, the Cuckoo in a tall birch at the edge of the wood, and the Black Grouse on the heather moor above the farm. The fence is a Norwegian skigard: grey poles laid slanting between pairs of upright stakes. The birds and the cow are natural animals without clothes.

The Black Grouse has stepped between them and raises one wing high like a judge calling for order, his lyre-shaped tail fanned and his red brows lifted. The Rooster and the Cuckoo stop mid-squawk and look up at him. Behind them the Cow looks on, calmly chewing.

Create one new illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: On the dewy grass by the split-rail fence, in the first rays of sunrise, the Rooster and the Cuckoo stand beak to beak with their feathers bristling, in the middle of their quarrel. The Black Grouse has stepped between them and raises one wing high like a judge calling for order, his lyre-shaped tail fanned and his red brows lifted. The Rooster and the Cuckoo stop mid-squawk and look up at him. Behind them the Cow looks on, calmly chewing.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Black Grouse: A large, calm black grouse cock, a little bigger than the rooster, with glossy blue-black plumage, a bright-red fleshy arch like an eyebrow above each eye, a white bar across each wing, a fluffy snow-white puff of feathers under his tail, and a lyre-shaped tail whose two outer feathers curl outwards like hooks. He has feathered grey legs, a short black beak and wise, kind dark eyes, and stands tall and dignified like a judge.
- the Rooster: A sleek, swaggering farmyard rooster with jet-black plumage that shimmers beetle-green in the light, a tall, jagged scarlet comb standing straight up, long dangling scarlet wattles, small white earlobes, fiery orange eyes, a sharp slate-grey beak, slate-grey legs with long spurs, and a fountain of long, curving green-black sickle feathers for a tail. He holds his head high and his chest puffed out.
- the Cuckoo: A slim, sleek common cuckoo, much smaller than the rooster, with a smooth ash-blue-grey head, back and wings, a white belly finely barred with thin dark stripes, a long, rounded dark-grey tail edged with little white spots, bright yellow rings around his round, sleepy eyes, a short, slightly curved dark beak with a yellow base and small yellow feet. One tuft of feathers always sticks up at the back of his head.
- the Cow: A gentle, sturdy old Norwegian farm cow with a glossy reddish-brown coat, a broad white stripe running along her back and down her tail, a white belly, white-speckled legs, a pink nose, big, calm brown eyes with long dark lashes and two short, pale, upward-curving horns. A small brass bell hangs from a leather strap around her neck. She chews her cud slowly and never hurries.

Setting:
- the Hill Farm: A small, poor hill farm at the edge of a birch-and-spruce wood: a low grey log cowshed with a turf roof and a small hatch high in its wall, a grey split-rail fence of slanting poles along a dewy meadow, a tall white birch whose lowest branch reaches out over the fence, and a slope of heather and bog rising behind towards a bare moor and a dark spruce ridge.

Story world: Old rural Norway, where the birds of farm, forest and moor can talk. The Rooster, the Cuckoo and the Black Grouse have bought one cow together and agreed that whoever wakes first in the morning shall have her. She grazes the meadow of a small hill farm at the edge of a birch-and-spruce wood. The Rooster lives in the hen loft of the cowshed, the Cuckoo in a tall birch at the edge of the wood, and the Black Grouse on the heather moor above the farm. The fence is a Norwegian skigard: grey poles laid slanting between pairs of upright stakes. The birds and the cow are natural animals without clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: A cold, clear May dawn: pale primrose and rose light rising over a dark spruce ridge, grey dew on the grass, the first tiny mouse-ear leaves on the birches, thin mist in the hollows and long blue shadows. Accents: the Rooster's scarlet comb, the Black Grouse's red brows and the Cow's russet coat.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

The birds wear no clothes, and the hen goes barefoot.

Picture: On a long summer road winding over green hills, the Dressed-up Cat runs ahead with her tail straight up and her red feathered hat at a jaunty angle. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Dressed-up Cat: A clever, dignified grey tabby cat, a little larger than an ordinary farm cat, with dark silver-grey stripes, four snow-white paws, a white chest, big green-gold eyes, long white whiskers and her old faded red leather collar, now dressed for visiting: a small red hat with a curling white feather set at a jaunty angle between her ears, and a little moss-green cloak fastened at her throat with a tiny brass clasp. She walks and sits upright and proud, her striped tail held high.
- Sir Per: A lanky young man of about nineteen with a long neck, a kind oval face, soft brown eyes, a straight nose, a shy smile and chestnut hair tied back in a short ponytail, dressed as a fine lord and standing a little taller than before. He wears a bright green velvet jacket with rows of gold buttons and gold braid, a flowing scarlet cape fastened with a gold clasp, a broad-brimmed hat with a long curling white feather, cream breeches and tall brown riding boots.

Setting:
- the Silver Castle: A great castle made all of polished silver, with slender towers and steep silver roofs, standing on a green rise in a wide summer landscape and shining so brightly in the sun that it hurts the eyes. In front of it, three tall arched gates stand one behind the other across the road: the first of brass, the second of silver and the third of gold, each between two thick stone gateposts. Across a meadow opposite the gates rises a low wooded ridge.

Story world: Old rural Norway in high summer. Per's parents' tiny grey log cottage stands empty at the edge of a spruce forest. Characters

Per per · Per

Den yngste sønnen som arver katten og blir kjent som «Herreper» når han følger kattens plan.

A gangly, gentle young man of about nineteen with a long neck, long arms, a kind oval face, soft brown eyes, a straight nose, a shy smile and chestnut hair tied back in a short ponytail. He wears a grey homespun coat far too big for him, its sleeves rolled up and its elbows mended, over a washed-out blue smock, baggy brown trousers tucked into cracked old boots tied with string, and a shapeless oatmeal knitted cap.

Herreper herreper · Sir Per

Per i de fine klærne som katten skaffet ham. Alt kongen viser ham, sier han at han har mye finere hjemme.

A lanky young man of about nineteen with a long neck, a kind oval face, soft brown eyes, a straight nose, a shy smile and chestnut hair tied back in a short ponytail, dressed as a fine lord and standing a little taller than before. He wears a bright green velvet jacket with rows of gold buttons and gold braid, a flowing scarlet cape fastened with a gold clasp, a broad-brimmed hat with a long curling white feather, cream breeches and tall brown riding boots.

Katten katten · the Cat

En smart katt som legger en plan, skaffer gaver til kongen, narrer et troll og viser seg å være en forhekset prinsesse.

A clever, dignified grey tabby cat, a little larger than an ordinary farm cat, with dark silver-grey stripes, four snow-white paws, a white chest and chin, big green-gold eyes, long white whiskers and a long striped tail that she carries high. Around her neck she wears an old, worn collar of faded red leather with a small tarnished brass buckle. She sits very upright, like a small queen.

Katten i hatt og kappe katten-pyntet · the Dressed-up Cat

Katten i sin egen fjærhatt og lille kappe. Hun springer foran vogna, deler ut kongens sølv og vet alltid hva som skal skje.

A clever, dignified grey tabby cat, a little larger than an ordinary farm cat, with dark silver-grey stripes, four snow-white paws, a white chest, big green-gold eyes, long white whiskers and her old faded red leather collar, now dressed for visiting: a small red hat with a curling white feather set at a jaunty angle between her ears, and a little moss-green cloak fastened at her throat with a tiny brass clasp. She walks and sits upright and proud, her striped tail held high.

Kongen kongen · the King

Mottar gavene, blir nysgjerrig på Herreper og drar for å se om rikdommen hans er ekte.

A short, very fat king of about sixty with a round, shiny bald head, bulging cheeks, a red nose, small beady eyes, a grumpy look and a huge drooping grey walrus moustache that hides his mouth. A small gold crown sits right on top of his bald head. He wears a long purple wool robe with a spotted ermine collar, stretched tight over his enormous belly, a wide gold belt, white stockings and pointed red leather shoes.

Trollet trollet · the Troll

Eieren av slottet som truer inntrengerne, men blir lurt til å se sola og sprekker.

A colossal old troll about four times a man's height, round-shouldered and heavy, covered all over in long, matted, oatmeal-beige fur like a giant unshorn ram, with heather and twigs caught in it. Two round yellow eyes glow like lanterns above a big potato nose, and his broad, soft mouth shows two blunt buck teeth. He has little round ears, great grey hands like stone, a long cow's tail with a tuft at the end and broad, hairy bare feet.

Prinsessa prinsessa · the Princess

Blir fri fra trollets forbannelse når katten mister hodet, og kan bli Herreper sin dronning.

A graceful young woman of about nineteen with a small pointed chin, high cheekbones, almond-shaped green-gold eyes like a cat's, a little upturned nose and very long, straight golden hair falling to her knees, with one silver-grey streak at her left temple. She wears a dove-grey silk gown with snow-white cuffs, a white lace collar and fine silver embroidery at the hem, and a thin silver circlet on her brow.

#05 · jenta
simplified · after paragraph 23
Like ved lå et slott. Tidlig om morgenen kom en tjenestejente derfra for å hente vann i kilden til prinsens te. Hun bøyde seg over vannet og fikk se det vakre ansiktet der nede, og hun trodde det var hennes eget. Så slengte hun fra seg bøtta, gikk hjem, slo med nakken og sa:

«Er jeg så vakker, så er jeg for god til å gå og bære vann.»

- the Blue Bull: A huge, powerful bull, taller at the shoulder than a grown man, with a glossy, deep cornflower-blue coat that always looks freshly polished, a paler blue-grey muzzle, big, soft dark-brown eyes with long lashes, two long, smooth cream-white horns curving forwards and up, large soft ears, a curly tuft of darker blue hair between the horns, a long tail ending in a navy-blue tassel, and dark grey hooves. Calm, wise and kind.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The princess grows up at her father's palace, a long, dark timber hall with turf roofs, a byre and forest pastures climbing to the blue fells. The Blue Bull keeps a small, folded white cloth in his left ear; spread on the grass, it sets itself with food. Far away lie three magic woods, one of copper, one of silver and one of gold, where every trunk, leaf and flower is metal and gold drips from the leaves. Each troll wears a curved cow horn of healing ointment at its belt. At the journey's end, a sheer grey cliff looks down on a great castle of pale-grey stone with green copper roofs and a tarred stave church close by. In the castle, a steep, dark oak staircase climbs from the sooty kitchen to the Prince's chamber. The gold shoes are small, pointed and shining.

This story's season, light and colours: Cool, clear early autumn under high, pale-blue skies: blue-grey fells, birches turning yellow and purple heather, with the bull's deep, glossy blue as the strongest colour until the magic woods blaze in polished copper, frosty silver and molten gold. The castle kitchen is dim, sooty and firelit; the church Sundays are bright, windy and fresh.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
