Characters

Kongedatteren prinsessa · the King's Daughter

Kongens snille datter, som stemoren sulter og setter til å gjete kyrne, og som får en trofast venn i den blå oksen.

A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair tied back loosely with a strip of blue cloth. She wears a faded, much-mended dress of pale sage-green wool with thin gold trim at the neck and cuffs, a grey knitted shawl and worn brown leather shoes, and carries a small birch-bark basket on her arm.

Kari Trestakk (kongedatteren) kari-trestakk · Kari Woodsmock

En snill og modig kongedatter som blir gjort til tjenestejente og skjuler seg i en trestakk, men beholder styrken til å overleve og finne veien til et nytt liv.

A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, her face and hands black with soot and her long, wavy copper hair in a messy braid dulled with ash. Over a plain grey linen shift she wears the wooden smock: a stiff, bell-shaped garment of thin, grey-brown wooden boards laced together like the staves of a barrel, reaching from her neck to her ankles, and wooden clogs.

Kari i kobberkjolen kari-kobberkjole · Kari in the Copper Dress

Kari den første søndagen, i en kjole like blank som kobberskogen, på vei til kirken til hest.

A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair falling loose down her back under a thin copper band. She wears a long, flowing gown of shining copper cloth that glows warm orange-pink like polished copper, embroidered with small copper leaves, with long copper-coloured gloves and soft copper slippers.

Kari i sølvkjolen kari-solvkjole · Kari in the Silver Dress

Kari den andre søndagen, i en kjole sydd med sølv over det hele, på en hest med sølvbrodert sal.

A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair in one loose braid woven with silver ribbons. She wears a long gown stitched all over with silver thread that glitters like frost, trimmed with rows of tiny silver leaves, a short silver-grey riding cape and silver slippers, and carries a slim riding whip with a silver handle.

Kari i gullkjolen kari-gullkjole · Kari in the Gold Dress

Kari den tredje søndagen, i en kjole av nesten bare gull og diamanter, med små sko av gull.

A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair flowing loose under a slender gold band. She wears a long, full gown of gold cloth sewn all over with small sparkling diamonds that glitter like dew, and two small, pointed shoes of shining gold.

Den blå oksen blaa-oksen · the Blue Bull

En stor, blank blå okse som hjelper Kari med mat og redder henne fra stemoren, og som kjemper mot trollene i metallskogene.

A huge, powerful bull, taller at the shoulder than a grown man, with a glossy, deep cornflower-blue coat that always looks freshly polished, a paler blue-grey muzzle, big, soft dark-brown eyes with long lashes, two long, smooth cream-white horns curving forwards and up, large soft ears, a curly tuft of darker blue hair between the horns, a long tail ending in a navy-blue tassel, and dark grey hooves. Calm, wise and kind.

Stemoren (dronningen) dronninga · the Queen

En misunnelig og hard dronning som plager Kari og legger planer for å bli kvitt den blå oksen.

A tall, thin queen of about forty with a long, pinched face, a sharp pointed nose, narrow pale-green eyes, thin arched eyebrows, a small mouth turned down at the corners and jet-black hair scraped into a tight bun under a tall, spiky silver crown. She wears a stiff, high-collared gown of dark slate-grey wool with a narrow white linen collar, a black velvet cloak and many heavy rings, and holds a white linen handkerchief.

Datteren til dronningen dronningens-datter · the Stepsister

Dronningens datter, like stygg og slem som kongedatteren er snill og vakker. Hun får gullskoen på og blir pyntet til brud.

A gangly young woman of about eighteen with a long, sour face, a pinched, turned-up nose, small squinting pale-green eyes, a pouting mouth and thin, straw-pale hair in two stiff braids that stick out sideways. She wears an over-trimmed dress of sour gooseberry-green wool covered in far too many pink ribbons, white stockings and pointed green shoes on very long, big feet.

Prinsen prinsen · the Prince

En stolt prins som først avviser Kari i trestakken, men blir dypt betatt av den ukjente jenta i de skinnende kjolene og leter etter henne med gullskoen.

A broad-shouldered prince of about twenty-two with a proud, stubborn face, a strong jaw, a slightly hooked nose, bright blue eyes under straight fair brows and thick, wavy honey-blond hair swept back from his forehead and falling to his collar, under a small gold crown. He wears a heather-purple wool tunic with gold trim over a cream linen shirt, a short dark-green cloak fastened with a round gold brooch, black hose and soft black leather boots.

Mannen i berget mannen-i-berget · the Old Man of the Mountain

En mann som kommer ut av bergveggen når Kari banker på med kjeppen, og som gir henne kjoler av kobber, sølv og gull og en hest å ri til kirken.

A small, sturdy old man no taller than a young girl, with a round, rosy, wrinkled face, a big round nose, twinkling bright-blue eyes under bushy white eyebrows and a long, silky white beard that reaches his knees. He wears a long, hooded moss-green cloak with a wooden toggle, a brown tunic with a rope belt and soft brown boots, and carries a small brass lantern that glows warm yellow.

Trollet med tre hoder trollet-med-tre-hoder · the Three-Headed Troll

Trollet som eier kobberskogen, og som kommer farende med alle tre hodene når kongedatteren river av et blad.

A squat, pot-bellied troll about twice as tall as a man, with pale, chalky grey-white skin like weathered limestone, speckled with grey freckles and patches of moss, short bandy legs and long dangling arms. It has three bald, egg-shaped heads on three thick necks, each with a big red bulbous nose, small round orange eyes, one crooked tooth and tufts of stiff orange hair behind the ears. It wears a ragged brown sacking kilt, with a curved cow horn of ointment hanging from its rope belt.

Trollet med seks hoder trollet-med-seks-hoder · the Six-Headed Troll

Trollet som eier sølvskogen. Det er dobbelt så sterkt som det første, og det slåss med oksen i tre hele døgn.

A tall, lanky troll about three times as tall as a man, with knobbly, rusty-orange skin like iron-stained rock, patched with grey lichen, long skinny arms and legs and huge flat feet. On a wide, bony pair of shoulders sit six small heads in a row, each with a long droopy nose, sleepy yellow eyes, big flappy ears and wispy white hair like bog cotton. It wears a moth-eaten grey wool tunic, with a curved cow horn of ointment on a string at its belt.

Trollet med ni hoder trollet-med-ni-hoder · the Nine-Headed Troll

Trollet som eier gullskogen, større og sterkere enn de to andre trollene til sammen. For hvert hode oksen stanger i hjel, blåser de andre liv i det igjen.

An enormous, pear-shaped troll as tall as six men, with lumpy skin the dusky pink and purple of blooming heather, a huge round belly and short, stumpy arms and legs like tree stumps. Along its broad shoulders sit nine small round heads in a row, each with puffy cheeks, a tiny snub nose, small black eyes under bushy grey brows, big round ears and a shock of spiky grey hair. It wears a huge patched brown hide tunic, with a curved cow horn of ointment hanging from its belt.

#02 · prinsessa, blaa-oksen
simplified · after paragraph 5
Hun stakk hånden inn i øret hans, og der lå duken, pent sammenbrettet. Hun bredte den ut på gresset, og med ett disket den opp med alt hun kunne ønske seg. Det dampet av varme fat, det sto vin og mjød i blanke krus, og det var søtkake så mye hun orket. Oksen sto tett ved siden av henne og så på at hun spiste.

Med ett disket duken opp med alt hun kunne ønske seg.

Alt: Kongedatteren kneler ved en hvit duk på gresset, dekket med dampende fat, brød og kaker. Den blå oksen står tett ved siden av og ser på at hun spiser.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The princess grows up at her father's palace, a long, dark timber hall with turf roofs, a byre and forest pastures climbing to the blue fells. The Blue Bull keeps a small, folded white cloth in his left ear; spread on the grass, it sets itself with food. Far away lie three magic woods, one of copper, one of silver and one of gold, where every trunk, leaf and flower is metal and gold drips from the leaves. Each troll wears a curved cow horn of healing ointment at its belt. At the journey's end, a sheer grey cliff looks down on a great castle of pale-grey stone with green copper roofs and a tarred stave church close by. In the castle, a steep, dark oak staircase climbs from the sooty kitchen to the Prince's chamber. The gold shoes are small, pointed and shining.

This story's season, light and colours: Cool, clear early autumn under high, pale-blue skies: blue-grey fells, birches turning yellow and purple heather, with the bull's deep, glossy blue as the strongest colour until the magic woods blaze in polished copper, frosty silver and molten gold. The castle kitchen is dim, sooty and firelit; the church Sundays are bright, windy and fresh.

The Prince stands before her, staring in wonder. Around the walls, twelve maids, servants and townsfolk gape with open mouths, their laughter gone. Light falls from tall windows.

Create one new illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: In the great hall of the castle, Kari in the Gold Dress stands in the middle of the floor, shining, with a gold shoe on each foot and the wooden smock lying in a heap of grey boards at her feet. The Prince stands before her, staring in wonder. Around the walls, twelve maids, servants and townsfolk gape with open mouths, their laughter gone. Light falls from tall windows.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Kari in the Gold Dress: A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair flowing loose under a slender gold band. She wears a long, full gown of gold cloth sewn all over with small sparkling diamonds that glitter like dew, and two small, pointed shoes of shining gold.
- the Prince: A broad-shouldered prince of about twenty-two with a proud, stubborn face, a strong jaw, a slightly hooked nose, bright blue eyes under straight fair brows and thick, wavy honey-blond hair swept back from his forehead and falling to his collar, under a small gold crown. He wears a heather-purple wool tunic with gold trim over a cream linen shirt, a short dark-green cloak fastened with a round gold brooch, black hose and soft black leather boots.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The princess grows up at her father's palace, a long, dark timber hall with turf roofs, a byre and forest pastures climbing to the blue fells. The Blue Bull keeps a small, folded white cloth in his left ear; spread on the grass, it sets itself with food. Far away lie three magic woods, one of copper, one of silver and one of gold, where every trunk, leaf and flower is metal and gold drips from the leaves. Each troll wears a curved cow horn of healing ointment at its belt. At the journey's end, a sheer grey cliff looks down on a great castle of pale-grey stone with green copper roofs and a tarred stave church close by. In the castle, a steep, dark oak staircase climbs from the sooty kitchen to the Prince's chamber. The gold shoes are small, pointed and shining.

This story's season, light and colours: Cool, clear early autumn under high, pale-blue skies: blue-grey fells, birches turning yellow and purple heather, with the bull's deep, glossy blue as the strongest colour until the magic woods blaze in polished copper, frosty silver and molten gold. The castle kitchen is dim, sooty and firelit; the church Sundays are bright, windy and fresh.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Alt: Tiny Littlecourt stands on the moonlit sand with his hand on his sword, looking out at a black ship in the mist. Behind him the princess sits on a stone, and Sir Red hides in a tree.

The Shore at dusk under a huge, low orange moon. Tiny Lillekort stands on the sand at the water's edge with his feet apart, one hand on the golden hilt of his sword and his little ship peeking out of his pocket, gazing boldly out to sea, where a black ship with black sails comes looming through the silver mist. Behind him, the Younger Princess, wrapped in a black mourning cloak, sits on the flat grey stone clasping her hands, and high in the great oak Sir Red peers out between the leaves.

Picture: The Shore at dusk under a huge, low orange moon. Tiny Lillekort stands on the sand at the water's edge with his feet apart, one hand on the golden hilt of his sword and his little ship peeking out of his pocket, gazing boldly out to sea, where a black ship with black sails comes looming through the silver mist. Behind him, the Younger Princess, wrapped in a black mourning cloak, sits on the flat grey stone clasping her hands, and high in the great oak Sir Red peers out between the leaves.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Lillekort: A tiny, bold boy only days old but no bigger than a child of four, with the sturdy, natural proportions of a small child, a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined little chin and a mop of golden curls. An oversized knitted cap with blue-and-white stripes flops over one ear. He wears his big brothers' old rags: a far-too-big, much-patched grey-brown linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up, baggy patched brown breeches tied with string and big, worn-out leather shoes.
- the Younger Princess: A slim, lively princess of about eighteen with a round face, a pointed little chin, a small turned-up nose, big grey eyes, pale skin with pink cheeks and short, bouncy platinum-blonde curls. On her curls sits a small gold circlet shaped like a ring of oak leaves. She wears an emerald-green wool gown with long, narrow sleeves and a high round collar embroidered with tiny gold leaves, a thin gold belt and a string of small white pearls.
- Sir Red: A big, burly, barrel-chested knight of about forty, a head taller than most men, with a broad, puffy face that easily turns bright red, a big bulbous nose, small shifty pale-blue eyes under bushy brows, curly red hair and a huge, bushy fiery-red beard. He wears polished steel armour over a red tunic, a long bright-red cloak and heavy boots, and always has a big white handkerchief tucked into his belt.

Setting:
- the Shore: A wide, pale sandy beach below the royal manor, curving along the open sea. Right at the water's edge lies one big, flat, grey boulder, and at the top of the beach stands a huge, gnarled old oak with wide, spreading branches and yellow-brown autumn leaves. Tufts of beach grass grow in the low dunes, and a grassy slope rises behind to the dark log buildings of the manor.

Story world: Old rural Norway on the open coast, long ago. Lillekort and his twin are born in a wretched, crooked cottage with a sagging turf roof at the edge of a birch forest. Far away, the King's manor stands on a slope above a wide sandy shore by the open sea: dark log buildings with turf roofs around a long hall, all hung with black cloth while the princess is promised to three sea trolls, who come over the sea in black ships with black sails. Lillekort's sword has a golden hilt and a plain brown leather sheath. His magic ship is a wooden ship with two masts and white sails; when small, it fits in his pocket. The princess's three secret garments are of gold, silver and brass. The iron cable is a colossal chain. At the bottom of the sea stands a rock mountain with a door.

This story's season, light and colours: Late autumn on the open coast: blustery days with yellow birch leaves and scarlet rowan berries, and a dark-green sea with white-capped waves. The three Thursday evenings lie under a huge, low orange moon, with silver sea mist drifting over the sand. At the wedding, candlelight makes gold, silver and brass glitter. Under the sea: cold green-blue gloom and the red glow of the troll's oven.

Characters

Lillekort lillekort · Lillekort

En svært liten, men smart og fryktløs gutt som drar ut i verden og vinner magiske gaver, beseirer troll og ordner opp med både kongerike og kjærlighet.

A tiny, bold boy only days old but no bigger than a child of four, with the sturdy, natural proportions of a small child, a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined little chin and a mop of golden curls. An oversized knitted cap with blue-and-white stripes flops over one ear. He wears his big brothers' old rags: a far-too-big, much-patched grey-brown linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up, baggy patched brown breeches tied with string and big, worn-out leather shoes.

Lillekort i gulldrakten lillekort-gull · Lillekort in Gold

Lillekort i drakten av gull som kongsdattera trakk på ham mens han sov. Han skjuler den under fillene helt til bryllupet, og da lyser det av ham.

The same tiny, bold boy, no bigger than a child of four, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined little chin and a mop of golden curls under his oversized blue-and-white striped knitted cap. Now he wears a shining garment of pure gold that glows with its own light: a short, close-fitting gold tunic with a high collar and round gold buttons, gold hose and small gold shoes, with a golden-hilted sword in a plain brown sheath at his belt.

Kong Lavring kong-lavring · Lavring

Lillekorts tvillingbror, like av utseende, som kommer når han blir ropt på og til slutt hjelper til med å løse floken mellom de to prinsessene.

A tiny, bold boy only days old but no bigger than a child of four, with exactly the same round face, rosy cheeks, small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes and mop of golden curls as his twin brother, but with a cheeky, know-it-all grin. An oversized knitted cap with red-and-white stripes sits on his head. He wears his big brothers' old rags: a far-too-big, patched mustard-yellow wool jacket with the sleeves rolled up, baggy patched grey breeches tied with string and big wooden clogs.

Kong Lavring i Lillekorts klær kong-lavring-gull · Lavring in Gold

Kong Lavring i klærne til tvillingbroren, så lik at kongsdøtrene tror det er Lillekort som kommer.

The tiny twin dressed in his brother's clothes, so that nobody can tell the two apart: a bold boy no bigger than a child of four, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes and a mop of golden curls under an oversized blue-and-white striped knitted cap, in a shining garment of pure gold: a short, close-fitting gold tunic with a high collar and round gold buttons, gold hose and small gold shoes.

Kongsdattera (den yngste) prinsessa-yngste · the Younger Princess

Prinsessen som skal hentes av tre troll, men som blir reddet av Lillekort og hjelper ham med en plan som avslører den falske ridderen.

A slim, lively princess of about eighteen with a round face, a pointed little chin, a small turned-up nose, big grey eyes, pale skin with pink cheeks and short, bouncy platinum-blonde curls. On her curls sits a small gold circlet shaped like a ring of oak leaves. She wears an emerald-green wool gown with long, narrow sleeves and a high round collar embroidered with tiny gold leaves, a thin gold belt and a string of small white pearls.

Den eldste kongsdattera eldste-prinsessa · the Elder Princess

Kongens andre datter, som trollet tok med seg til berget på havets bunn. Der sitter hun og syr til Lillekort kommer, og hun er både større og sterkere enn søstera.

A tall, strong, broad-shouldered princess of about twenty-one, a head taller than her younger sister and quick on her feet, with a round face, a pointed chin, a small turned-up nose, big grey eyes, pink cheeks and thick platinum-blonde curls tumbling to her shoulders, held back with a string of pearls. She wears a long coral-red wool gown embroidered with little white seashells along the hem, a belt of plaited silver cord and a silver thimble on one finger.

Ridder Rød ridder-rod · Sir Red

En feig og ærekjær ridder som gjemmer seg når trollene kommer, og prøver å stjele æren for redningen ved trusler og løgn.

A big, burly, barrel-chested knight of about forty, a head taller than most men, with a broad, puffy face that easily turns bright red, a big bulbous nose, small shifty pale-blue eyes under bushy brows, curly red hair and a huge, bushy fiery-red beard. He wears polished steel armour over a red tunic, a long bright-red cloak and heavy boots, and always has a big white handkerchief tucked into his belt.

Kjerringa med ett øye kjerringa · the One-Eyed Hag

Ei gammel, gammel, krokrygget kjerring med bare ett øye. Lillekort møter tre slike, og for å få øyet igjen gir de ham et sverd, et skip og kunsten å brygge.

A tiny, ancient hag, no taller than a small child and bent double so that her back curves like a hook, with a small, deeply wrinkled face like a walnut, a flat little nose, a wide toothless mouth and only one eye: a single round, shiny sky-blue eye in the middle of her forehead. Her thin white hair is in a tiny knot. She wears a long, faded lavender homespun dress and a big brown fringed shawl, and leans on a crooked stick.

Kongen kongen · the King

Kongen på kongsgården ved havet, som har lovet bort den ene dattera til tre troll og mistet den andre til et troll i havet.

A jolly, stocky king of about sixty with a big round belly, a broad, ruddy face made for laughing, a bulbous nose, crinkly brown eyes, bushy chestnut-brown eyebrows, thick chestnut curls and a big, round, curly chestnut-brown beard clipped short like a bush. He wears a tall gold crown with seven points, each tipped with a round amber bead, a long rust-orange wool robe with a wide brown fur collar, a gold belt and soft brown boots.

Kokkejenta kokkejenta · the Kitchen Maid

Kokkejenta på kongsgården, som Lillekort bærer ved og vann for, og som får fang på fang med bånd av gull og sølv.

A sturdy, cheerful kitchen maid of about eighteen with a broad, rosy, round face, merry dark-brown eyes, a snub nose dusted with flour and thick black hair wound into a bun under a white linen kerchief. Her sleeves are rolled up over strong arms. She wears a long cornflower-blue homespun dress and a big white apron with soup stains, and keeps a large wooden ladle tucked into her apron strings.

Trollet med fem hoder trollet-fem · the Five-Headed Troll

Det første av de tre trollene som kongsdattera er lovet bort til. Det kommer farende over sjøen med fem hoder og ei tjukk jernstang.

A huge, bloated sea troll about five times as tall as a man, with dusky purple-grey skin like an old mussel shell, crusted with barnacles and hung with strands of dark seaweed, a great sagging belly, long dangling arms and flat, webbed feet. It has exactly five heads on five thick, wrinkled necks, each with a long drooping nose, small round yellow eyes and a tuft of shaggy grey hair. It wears a kilt of old brown fishing net and carries a thick iron bar.

Trollet med ti hoder trollet-ti · the Ten-Headed Troll

Det andre trollet som kommer for å hente kongsdattera, dobbelt så stort som det første og med ti hoder.

An enormous sea troll about ten times as tall as a man, with rough slate-blue skin, knobbly and shiny like wet rock, a broad, square body, short thick legs and huge webbed feet. It has exactly ten round heads in two rows of five, one row above the other, each with a flat nose, big goggling green eyes, a wide frog mouth and a scraggly grey beard. It wears a torn black sail wrapped around its middle and carries a huge iron bar.

Trollet med femten hoder trollet-femten · the Fifteen-Headed Troll

Det tredje og største trollet, med femten hoder og ei jernstang som får jorda til å sprute femten meter til værs.

The biggest sea troll of all, as tall as a hill, with dark peat-brown, lumpy skin like a bog, shaggy grey hair on its shoulders, a round belly and legs like old tree stumps. It has exactly fifteen heads stacked in a pyramid, five on its shoulders, then four, three, two and one on top, each with a round red nose, small blinking amber eyes and a shock of grey hair. It wears a huge patched sailcloth tunic tied with a ship's rope and carries a gigantic iron bar.

Trollet på havets bunn sjotrollet · the Undersea Troll

Trollet som har tatt den eldste kongsdattera med seg til berget på havets bunn. Det er så hissig og sint at det river folk i filler, men det vil gjerne ha sterkt øl til selskapet.

A fat, savage-tempered troll about three times as tall as a man, with smooth, shiny turquoise skin like a wet fish, a barrel belly, short bowed legs and big flat webbed feet. He has one huge head with a gigantic, wrinkly, trumpet-shaped nose that is always sniffing, bulging pale-orange eyes, bristly orange eyebrows and a long tangle of brown kelp for hair and beard. He wears baggy patched sailcloth breeches held up by a rope and a necklace of big shells.

Story world: Old rural Norway. At home: a small grey log farmhouse with a turf roof, a round stone well in the grass in front, and a small pigsty of rough grey planks. At the bottom of the well lies another world, where the well is only a dark stone arch in a grassy bank: a wide green meadow crossed by a low fence woven of brushwood, and a big old apple tree with a long pole against its trunk. Far beyond lies the troll farm, a big, dark old log farm with a cowshed and a well in the yard. The troll hag's daughter is a younger, slimmer copy of her mother with the same long hooked nose. The sieve is a big round wooden sieve. The three chests are small wooden chests with curved lids: one red, one green, and one blue with three little white crosses on its lid.

This story's season, light and colours: Two worlds. Above the well: a raw, overcast day at a poor farm, with wet grass and muted browns and greys. Below it: a strange, bright summer that never ends, with jewel-green grass, clover, buttercups and red apples under a pale, hazy sky; the troll farm in dark timber and deep shadow, lit by a small fire and by shafts of light in the cowshed. At the end, the pigsty glows with gold and silver. Accents: the Girl's blue headscarf and the red, green and blue chests.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Girl: A slender, kind girl of about sixteen, a little small for her age, with a narrow, gentle face, big grey eyes, a small nose, pink cheeks and a shy smile. Her light-brown wavy hair falls to her shoulders from under a blue linen headscarf knotted at the nape of her neck. She wears a plain, patched undyed linen dress, a faded brown apron and worn brown leather shoes.
- the Stepsister: A sturdy, broad-shouldered girl of about seventeen with a broad, square face, a heavy jaw, full lips pushed out in a sulk, a wide flat nose, small dark eyes under heavy black eyebrows drawn together in a scowl, and a big, bushy cloud of black frizzy hair tied on top with a red ribbon. She wears a fussy mustard-yellow wool dress with puffed sleeves and a ruffled white collar, red leather shoes with buckles and a small cloth pouch of raisins at her waist.
- the Stepmother: A short, stout, bossy farmwife of about forty-five with a big, doughy face, heavy cheeks, a small snub nose, small cold black eyes, a sour little mouth and frizzy black hair streaked with grey, bundled into a big knot on top of her head. She wears a stiff dark-plum wool dress with a black bodice and a starched white collar fastened with a large round silver brooch, and she usually stands with her arms folded.

Story world: Old rural Norway. At home: a small grey log farmhouse with a turf roof, a round stone well in the grass in front, and a small pigsty of rough grey planks. At the bottom of the well lies another world, where the well is only a dark stone arch in a grassy bank: a wide green meadow crossed by a low fence woven of brushwood, and a big old apple tree with a long pole against its trunk. Far beyond lies the troll farm, a big, dark old log farm with a cowshed and a well in the yard. The troll hag's daughter is a younger, slimmer copy of her mother with the same long hooked nose. The sieve is a big round wooden sieve. The three chests are small wooden chests with curved lids: one red, one green, and one blue with three little white crosses on its lid.

This story's season, light and colours: Two worlds. Above the well: a raw, overcast day at a poor farm, with wet grass and muted browns and greys. Below it: a strange, bright summer that never ends, with jewel-green grass, clover, buttercups and red apples under a pale, hazy sky; the troll farm in dark timber and deep shadow, lit by a small fire and by shafts of light in the cowshed. At the end, the pigsty glows with gold and silver. Accents: the Girl's blue headscarf and the red, green and blue chests.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

The farmer's three oxen are big, reddish-brown and white-faced, with short curved horns, and walk the Forest Road on a rope. The Bailiff lives at the Manor Farm: a white manor house, a kitchen with an open hearth and a spit, a long red stable of twelve stalls for his twelve dun fjord horses and a dark goose house full of white geese; he rides a big dapple-grey horse. The parson's vicarage has a great old maple in the garden. The barrel is a big oak barrel on a rickety two-wheeled cart, pulled by a bony old brown mare in a harness of willow withies and broom twigs.

Mestertyven (den yngste sønnen) mestertyven · the Master Thief

En smart og fryktløs ung mann som lærer røvernes «håndverk» og overgår alle med oppfinnsomme triks.

A wiry, nimble young man of about twenty-two with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, quick dark-brown eyes under arched eyebrows, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. Short curly black hair pokes out from under a small dark-grey felt hat with a narrow brim, worn tilted over one eye. He wears a long, patched bottle-green coat with deep pockets over a cream shirt, a red neckerchief, charcoal knee breeches and soft black boots.

Mestertyven i generaluniform mestertyven-general · the General

The master thief dressed up as a grand general: the same wiry young man of about twenty-two with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, a sly lopsided grin, a thin black moustache and short curly black hair. He wears a black two-cornered hat with a white plume, a dark-blue uniform coat with gold braid down the front, two rows of shiny brass buttons and gold-fringed epaulettes, a wide red sash, white breeches and tall polished black riding boots.

Once upon a time there was a cottager who had three sons. He had nothing to leave them and nothing to set them to, and no idea what to do with them either. So in the end he told them they could take up whatever trade they fancied and go wherever they pleased, and he would gladly walk them a little way. And so he did, until they came to a place where three roads met. There each son took a road of his own, and their father said goodbye and went home.

Where three roads met, each son took a road of his own.

Alt: The cottager stands where the road splits in three, waving goodbye. The two eldest sons walk off over the hill and along the river, and the youngest heads into the forest, looking back.

A wide view of a grey late-autumn morning where a dirt road splits into three: one road winds into a dark spruce forest, one climbs a bare hill and one follows a river. Seen from behind, the Cottager stands at the fork, wrapped in his striped blanket, one hand raised in farewell. His two elder sons, a tall young man and a stocky one, each with a small bundle on a stick, walk off along the hill road and the river road, while the Master Thief strides into the forest, glancing back.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Cottager: A thin, timid old cottager of about sixty-five with a long, droopy, worried face, big sad grey eyes under bushy brows, a red-tipped nose, sunken cheeks with grey stubble and thin grey hair sticking up in tufts. He wears a threadbare, patched mouse-brown smock tied with a cord, baggy patched breeches and old clogs, with a worn grey-and-blue striped blanket wrapped round his shoulders like a shawl.
- the Master Thief: A wiry, nimble young man of about twenty-two with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, quick dark-brown eyes under arched eyebrows, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. Short curly black hair pokes out from under a small dark-grey felt hat with a narrow brim, worn tilted over one eye. He wears a long, patched bottle-green coat with deep pockets over a cream shirt, a red neckerchief, charcoal knee breeches and soft black boots.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The cottager's tiny, crooked turf-roofed hut stands alone not far from where the road splits in three. Deep in a great spruce forest lies the robbers' big, dark timbered house with a blazing stone fireplace. The farmer's three oxen are big, reddish-brown and white-faced, with short curved horns, and walk the Forest Road on a rope. The Bailiff lives at the Manor Farm: a white manor house, a kitchen with an open hearth and a spit, a long red stable of twelve stalls for his twelve dun fjord horses and a dark goose house full of white geese; he rides a big dapple-grey horse. The parson's vicarage has a great old maple in the garden. The barrel is a big oak barrel on a rickety two-wheeled cart, pulled by a bony old brown mare in a harness of willow withies and broom twigs.

This story's season, light and colours: Late autumn: sleet-grey skies over wet, dark spruce forest, bare birches with a few last yellow leaves, frost-rimed mornings and muddy roads, and long, cold nights in deep blue moonlight lit by warm amber lanterns, candles and firelight. Accents: the thief's bottle-green, the Bailiff's canary yellow and the white of geese and bedsheets.

Picture: A bright, frosty morning on the front steps of the white manor house of the Manor Farm. The Bailiff, with a long-suffering sigh, puts his daughter's hand into the Master Thief's hand and pushes a fat leather purse of money at him with the other. The Bailiff's Daughter smiles at the Master Thief, who sweeps off his tilted hat and bows low.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Bailiff: A stout, self-important gentleman of about fifty-five with a huge round belly, a pink double chin, rosy jowls, small twinkling eyes, a snub nose, a neat grey moustache waxed into two curly tips and grey hair curling over his ears. He wears a round-crowned black hat, a tobacco-brown frock coat with brass buttons over a canary-yellow waistcoat stretched tight across his belly, a gold watch chain, grey striped trousers and shiny black shoes.
- the Bailiff's Daughter: A kind, clever young woman of about twenty with a heart-shaped face, a dimple in one cheek, lively grey-green eyes that always seem to be laughing, a small straight nose and nut-brown hair in two braids coiled into round buns over her ears. She wears a long apricot-coloured wool dress with puffed sleeves and a white collar embroidered with little sprigs of lily of the valley.
- the Master Thief: A wiry, nimble young man of about twenty-two with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, quick dark-brown eyes under arched eyebrows, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. Short curly black hair pokes out from under a small dark-grey felt hat with a narrow brim, worn tilted over one eye. He wears a long, patched bottle-green coat with deep pockets over a cream shirt, a red neckerchief, charcoal knee breeches and soft black boots.

Setting:
- the Manor Farm: A large, prosperous farm around a big yard with a stone well. On one side stands a grand two-storey manor house of white-painted timber with a dark hipped roof, rows of small-paned windows and a carved front door at the top of stone steps. Around the yard stand a long red stable with a wooden water trough by its door, a small dark goose house and a kitchen wing, with bare birches and a fenced garden behind.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The cottager's tiny, crooked turf-roofed hut stands alone not far from where the road splits in three. Deep in a great spruce forest lies the robbers' big, dark timbered house with a blazing stone fireplace. The farmer's three oxen are big, reddish-brown and white-faced, with short curved horns, and walk the Forest Road on a rope. The Bailiff lives at the Manor Farm: a white manor house, a kitchen with an open hearth and a spit, a long red stable of twelve stalls for his twelve dun fjord horses and a dark goose house full of white geese; he rides a big dapple-grey horse. The parson's vicarage has a great old maple in the garden. The barrel is a big oak barrel on a rickety two-wheeled cart, pulled by a bony old brown mare in a harness of willow withies and broom twigs.

This story's season, light and colours: Late autumn: sleet-grey skies over wet, dark spruce forest, bare birches with a few last yellow leaves, frost-rimed mornings and muddy roads, and long, cold nights in deep blue moonlight lit by warm amber lanterns, candles and firelight. Accents: the thief's bottle-green, the Bailiff's canary yellow and the white of geese and bedsheets.

Alt: The Rooster races towards us along the path through the Hazelwood with his wings out. Behind him, the Hen lies in the moss under a hazel bush, watching him go.

Behind him, under a hazel bush heavy with ripe nuts, the Hen lies in the moss among broken shells, watching him go. The path winds away between the bushes towards a sunny meadow.

A narrow winding path leads out between the bushes towards open fields.

Story world: Old rural Norway, at harvest time. The Hazelwood is a small, sunny wood of tall hazel bushes heavy with ripe nuts, on a hillside above a farming village. Just outside it, a clear, cold spring bubbles up between mossy stones and splashes into a little pool below a huge old linden tree. From there, paths run along the edge of the wood and down to the village: turf-roofed log farms, a barn with a threshing floor, a sow's muddy pen by a fence, a woodpile at the edge of the spruce forest and a small smithy. Deep in the forest lies the charcoal burner's clearing with its smoking, earth-covered kiln. The red-gold ribbons are narrow red silk ribbons woven with gold thread.

Accents: the Rooster's scarlet comb, the red-gold ribbons and the Virgin Mary's light blue. In the forest: dark spruce and drifting blue-grey kiln smoke.

Characters

Hanen hanen · the Rooster

En rask og sta hane som nekter å gi opp før han har skaffet vann til høna si.

A proud, sturdy farmyard rooster, snow-white all over with glossy white feathers, a big, floppy, bright scarlet comb and red wattles, a short yellow beak, round, earnest black eyes, strong yellow legs with spurs and a tall, arching tail of long white plumes. He carries himself upright with his chest puffed out, full of courage, and runs with his wings half spread.

Tuppe (Høna) hona · the Hen

Høna som får et nøtteskall i halsen og trenger hjelp før det er for sent.

A small, round, plump little hen, speckled grey all over with tiny white and charcoal flecks like salt and pepper, with a small neat red comb, a short pale beak, bright round orange eyes, soft fluffy grey feathers on her legs and little grey feet. She has a cheerful, curious, nut-loving look.

Kilden kilden · the Spring

En streng, men rettferdig kilde som bare gir vann når den får det den ber om.

A small, round, crystal-clear spring welling up between mossy grey stones and splashing down into a little pool about as wide as a cartwheel, fringed with ferns and blue forget-me-nots. In its bubbling surface a face can just be seen in the ripples: two round, shining bubble eyes and a wide, gurgling mouth. The water is so clear that the pebbles on the bottom glint.

Lindetreet linden · the Linden

Et stort lindetre som krever røde gullbånd før det vil gi fra seg løv.

An enormous, ancient linden tree with a broad, rounded crown of heart-shaped leaves, green with the first touches of yellow, a thick, gnarled grey-brown trunk and big knobbly roots like toes. In the bark of the trunk is a kind, sleepy old face: two knot-hole eyes under mossy bark eyebrows, a round knobbly nose and a wide, gentle mouth, and two low branches bend like arms.

Jomfru Maria jomfru-maria · the Virgin Mary

En rolig skikkelse som kan gi røde gullbånd, men først vil ha sko.

A small, soft, grandmotherly woman of about seventy with a round, kind, wrinkled face, twinkling light-grey eyes, a gentle smile and silver hair under a simple white linen veil. She wears a light-blue wool shawl over a plain, long lavender dress and goes barefoot. She looks like a humble country grandmother, with no halo and no crown.

Kullbrenneren kullbrenneren · the Charcoal Burner

Den sotsvarte kullbrenneren inne i skogen. Han er den eneste som ikke vil ha noe tilbake, for han synes synd på hanen.

A tall, lean, kindly man of about sixty, black with soot from his hood to his boots, so that only his friendly pale-blue eyes and a white-toothed smile shine out of a long, sooty face with a hooked nose and grey stubble. He wears a pointed grey wool hood over his head and shoulders, a long patched leather apron, sooty brown trousers and heavy boots.

Story world: Old rural Norway at sowing time, in the Ringerike country. The Farmer and his Wife have a small, poor farm with one brown field. A dusty road leads to the market town, where the Butcher has his shop and yard. Far along the roads stand a brand-new log house with no windows that still smells of resin, a small plain cottage, and a big farm with a storehouse and a field being ploughed. The Wife's hen is a scrawny, half-bald speckled hen. The widow's blue horse is a sturdy blue-grey dappled horse with a black mane and tail, harnessed to a small two-wheeled wooden cart; Per the Third's horse is chestnut-brown. The sieve is a big, round, shallow sieve with a wooden rim.

This story's season, light and colours: Late April at sowing time: a dry, breezy spring with pale sunshine and drifting cloud, bare brown fields and fresh dark furrows, birches in their first mouse-ear green, the last grey snow patches in the shade of the spruce, yellow coltsfoot in the ditches and dusty roads. At the end, a heavy grey sky that promises rain. Accents: the Wife's rust-orange skirt, white feathers and the blue-grey horse.

Kona kona · the Wife

Sta og lettlurt, havner i trøbbel når hun skal selge kua, og blir så forvirret at hun ikke kjenner seg selv igjen.

A cheerful, dreamy farm wife of about forty-five, a little round, with a long ski-jump nose, big round blue eyes that always look amazed, rosy cheeks, a pleased little smile and two long, thin straw-yellow plaits tied at the ends with red wool. She wears a rust-orange wool skirt, a black bodice laced with red ribbon over a white blouse with wide sleeves, a big white apron with one deep front pocket and wooden-soled shoes.

Kona med tjære og fjær kona-med-fjaer · the Feathered Wife

The Wife after the Butcher's prank: the same cheerful woman of about forty-five with a long ski-jump nose, big round amazed blue eyes and two long straw-yellow plaits tied with red wool, in her rust-orange skirt, black laced bodice and white apron, but now sticky with black tar and covered from head to toe with fluffy white, grey and brown feathers on her clothes, arms, hair and cheeks, so that she looks like a big, ruffled bird.

Mannen fra Ringerike mannen · the Farmer

En fattig, men kvikk bonde som bruker vett og frekke løgner for å skaffe penger og komme seg ut av knipa.

A lean, wiry farmer of about forty-five with a narrow, clever face, a long straight nose, lively dark eyes with laugh crinkles, a patient half-smile, a short, neat black beard and cropped black hair. He wears a small black cap with a turned-up brim, a faded cornflower-blue coat with big pockets and brass buttons, and patched grey trousers tucked into worn brown boots.

Slakteren slakteren · the Butcher

En slu bymann som utnytter konas dumskap, byr på mat og brennevin og lurer henne skikkelig.

A huge, barrel-chested butcher of about fifty with a round, shiny red face, a bulbous nose, twinkling little black eyes, bushy black eyebrows, a sly grin and a big, round, bushy black beard. He wears a small white linen cap, a red shirt with the sleeves rolled up over thick arms and a long white apron with blue stripes, and he always has a string of sausages slung over one shoulder.

Kjerringa som vil bære inn sol soldkjerringa · the Sieve Woman

Ei kjerring i ei ny tømmerstue uten vinduer, som springer ut og inn med ei sil for å bære inn sola.

A tiny, quick, bird-like woman of about thirty with a small round face, a pointed chin, bright eager green eyes, rosy cheeks and a mass of glossy black curls tied up in a sunflower-yellow kerchief. She wears an apricot-orange dress with a white apron and red shoes, and she always carries a big, round, shallow sieve with a wooden rim and a bottom full of tiny holes.

Kjerringa på gården enka · the Widow

Ei godtroende kjerring som har vært gift tre ganger, hver gang med en Per. Hun hører «Himmerike» når mannen sier Ringerike, og sender klær, sølvpenger og hest til Per den andre i himmelen.

A tall, big, well-fed farm wife of about sixty with a large round face, a double chin, pink cheeks, a big mouth always open to talk, bright little inquisitive eyes and iron-grey ringlets under a large round black bonnet trimmed with lace and tied under her chins. She wears a wine-red wool dress with silver buttons and a green silk shawl, and she always holds a long brass ear trumpet to one ear.

Per den tredje per · Per the Third

Kjerringas tredje mann, en gretten bonde som setter etter mannen fra Ringerike, men blir lurt til å ligge og stirre opp i skyene.

A tall, heavy, grumpy farmer of about fifty with a long, sour face, a drooping lower lip, a big red nose, deep frown lines, bristly black eyebrows and a short, stiff iron-grey beard like a doormat. He wears a floppy black stocking cap, a patched leather jerkin over a rust-red shirt, brown knee breeches and tall muddy boots.

She wears a rust-orange wool skirt, a black bodice laced with red ribbon over a white blouse with wide sleeves, a big white apron with one deep front pocket and wooden-soled shoes.

Setting:
- the Little Farm: A small, poor farm on a gentle slope: a low grey log cottage with a turf roof, a tiny cowshed, and a little storehouse standing on four stone legs with a steep roof of wooden shingles. In front lies one small brown field ringed by a split-rail fence, with a few birches in their first spring leaf and yellow coltsfoot along the fence.

Story world: Old rural Norway at sowing time, in the Ringerike country. The Farmer and his Wife have a small, poor farm with one brown field. A dusty road leads to the market town, where the Butcher has his shop and yard. Far along the roads stand a brand-new log house with no windows that still smells of resin, a small plain cottage, and a big farm with a storehouse and a field being ploughed. The Wife's hen is a scrawny, half-bald speckled hen. The widow's blue horse is a sturdy blue-grey dappled horse with a black mane and tail, harnessed to a small two-wheeled wooden cart; Per the Third's horse is chestnut-brown. The sieve is a big, round, shallow sieve with a wooden rim.

This story's season, light and colours: Late April at sowing time: a dry, breezy spring with pale sunshine and drifting cloud, bare brown fields and fresh dark furrows, birches in their first mouse-ear green, the last grey snow patches in the shade of the spruce, yellow coltsfoot in the ditches and dusty roads. At the end, a heavy grey sky that promises rain. Accents: the Wife's rust-orange skirt, white feathers and the blue-grey horse.

A grassy track leads from the pasture down into the birch forest. Her butter churn is a tall, narrow wooden churn with dark hoops and a long wooden dasher sticking out of its lid. The wolf and the fox look like real animals, apart from the fox's little pouch; the bear walks upright with a crook and a bag.

Reven reven · the Fox

En listig rev som lokker pent, får jobben som gjeter og spiser opp alle dyra.

A fox with glossy golden-orange fur the colour of marigolds, a creamy-white bib and cheeks, dark-brown lower legs and feet, big ears lined with cream fur, large, round honey-brown eyes with an innocent look, a short muzzle and a sweet smile. His full, fluffy golden-orange tail has a sooty black end. A thin strap across his breast holds a little brown leather shepherd's pouch.

Bjørnen bjornen · the Bear

En stor bjørn som gjerne vil bli gjeter, men som brøler så trærne rister når han skal lokke på dyra.

A huge bear with thick, shaggy honey-blond fur, paler cream fur on his muzzle and belly, a wide round face, small half-moon ears, a shiny black nose, small kind brown eyes and a tuft of fur sticking up on top of his head. He stands upright on his hind legs like a man and carries a long wooden shepherd's crook and a worn leather shoulder bag.

Ulven ulven · the Wolf

Sulten og truende, men får ikke jobben fordi ulingen hans ikke virker trygg.

A lanky, long-legged grey wolf with shaggy smoke-grey fur, darker along his back and pale silver on his chest and legs, a long, narrow muzzle, pale yellow eyes, tall pointed ears with the left one bent over at the tip, and a thin bushy tail held low. He wears a polite, awkward, closed-mouth smile and looks gangly rather than fierce.

english · after paragraph 19
The Fox sat up straight. “Dil—dal—holom!” he sang, so clear and sweet.

“Dil—dal—holom!” he sang, so clear and sweet.

Alt: The fox sits up straight on a boulder with his tail curled round his paws, singing. The woman stands on the track with her stick, her face lighting up.

On a grassy track where the mountain pasture meets the birch forest, on a clear, cool morning, the Fox sits up very straight on a mossy boulder with his black-tipped tail curled neatly around his paws, his snout raised and his eyes half closed, singing sweetly. The Farm Wife stands on the track leaning on her birch stick, her stern face lighting up with delight. Red dwarf birch and golden grass line the track, with blue ridges far away.

Create one new illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: On a grassy track where the mountain pasture meets the birch forest, on a clear, cool morning, the Fox sits up very straight on a mossy boulder with his black-tipped tail curled neatly around his paws, his snout raised and his eyes half closed, singing sweetly. The Farm Wife stands on the track leaning on her birch stick, her stern face lighting up with delight. Red dwarf birch and golden grass line the track, with blue ridges far away.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Fox: A fox with glossy golden-orange fur the colour of marigolds, a creamy-white bib and cheeks, dark-brown lower legs and feet, big ears lined with cream fur, large, round honey-brown eyes with an innocent look, a short muzzle and a sweet smile. His full, fluffy golden-orange tail has a sooty black end. A thin strap across his breast holds a little brown leather shepherd's pouch.
- the Farm Wife: A strong, broad-shouldered farm woman of about forty with a wide, sun-browned face, a broad nose, sharp blue eyes under straight black eyebrows and a firm, no-nonsense mouth; her black hair is tucked under a dark-red kerchief knotted at the nape. She wears a dark-green wool dress with rolled-up sleeves, a blue-and-white checked apron, a wide leather belt and sturdy leather shoes, and carries a long, white-barked birch stick.

Story world: Old rural Norway, where the animals can talk. The woman keeps her animals at a mountain summer farm high up where the birch forest ends: a small grey log hut with a turf roof and a stone doorstep, a little cowshed and a split-rail fence around a green pasture, with a stony stream below and a grove of birches beyond it. A grassy track leads from the pasture down into the birch forest. Her butter churn is a tall, narrow wooden churn with dark hoops and a long wooden dasher sticking out of its lid. The wolf and the fox look like real animals, apart from the fox's little pouch; the bear walks upright with a crook and a bag.

This story's season, light and colours: Late August at a mountain summer farm, when the fells take on their first autumn colours: deep-red dwarf birch and golden grass on the slopes, ripe blueberries, blue ridges far away and clear, cool air. The evening glows orange and rose over the mountains. Accents: dwarf-birch red, the fox's golden orange and the white of the cream.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.

- Draw each named character only once.

Rike-Per Kremmer rigeper · 18/18 pictures

Møllergutten må skaffe tre fjær av stjerten på Dragen av Dybenfart.

Alt: Om natten sover Dragen i ei diger seng, og stjerten med tre skinnende gullfjær ligger i en bue over gulvet. Under senga kikker møllergutten fram og holder pusten.

The miller's lad must fetch three feathers from the tail of the Dragon of Deep-Ford.

Alt: At night the dragon sleeps in an enormous bed, his tail with three shining golden feathers curling across the floor. From under the bed, the miller's lad peers out, holding his breath.

Night in the Castle Hall, lit only by the red embers of the hearth. The Dragon sleeps in his enormous bed, snoring, a thread of grey smoke rising from his nostrils, and his long tail hangs over the edge and curls across the flagstones towards the viewer, ending in three long, shining golden feathers. From the dark space under the bed, the Miller's Lad peers out at the feathers, holding his breath. Heaps of gold glint along the walls.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Miller's Lad: A sturdy, broad-shouldered lad of about nineteen with a round, open, honest face, a button nose, friendly pale-blue eyes, a wide, warm grin and short, tight strawberry-blond curls. He wears a floppy, wide-brimmed dove-grey felt hat with a broad scarlet band, a loose white smock-shirt tied at the neck, a short oatmeal jerkin, moss-brown trousers tucked into thick ankle socks, and sturdy wooden clogs.
- the Dragon: An ancient, heavy, pot-bellied dragon about twice as tall as a man, who walks upright on short, thick hind legs with big blunt claws. He has bumpy plum-purple scales dulled with age, a pale lavender belly, small leathery wings far too small for him, a long snout with round nostrils trailing grey smoke, big heavy-lidded amber eyes and a row of rust-orange spikes down his back. His long tail ends in exactly three long, shining golden feathers.

Setting:
- the Castle Hall: A huge, gloomy hall in a black stone castle, with rough dark walls, a high vaulted roof and small, deep-set windows. A big open hearth burns with a log fire, and above it a huge old two-handed sword hangs on an iron hook. Against one wall stands an enormous dragon-sized bed with dark-red covers and a deep, dark space beneath it, with a small plain bed beside it; a long plank table, a cupboard set into the wall, and heaps of gold and silver along the walls.

Story world: Old rural Norway, over many years. Rich Per the pedlar's big farm lies above a river; just below it stands a small grey log mill, and many miles downstream a second, older mill with a big wooden waterwheel. The chest is a small, finely made box of polished dark wood with brass corners, its seams sealed with black pitch and an iron key in the lock. Per's letters are folded papers sealed with red wax. The robbers' farm is a shabby log farmhouse deep in a dark spruce forest; the young couple's farm lies up under a bare ridge. The royal manors are clusters of dark log halls with carved gables. Far away runs a great, wide river with no boat or bridge, and on the steep bank above it stands a big black stone castle. The three feathers are long, shining golden feathers.

This story's season, light and colours: Early winter in the river valleys: black, fast, ice-cold rivers with low mist hanging over them, the first thin snow on the banks and fields, frosted reeds and bare birches and alders under iron-grey skies, and short, pale afternoons fading into long blue dusks. Indoors: amber lamplight and firelight. In the black castle: slate-dark gloom, ember-red firelight and the glint of heaped gold.

Characters

Møllergutten mollergutten · the Miller's Lad

En fattig gutt som blir kastet ut i elva som spedbarn, vokser opp til å bli modig og heldig, og ender med å vinne både brud og rikdom.

A sturdy, broad-shouldered lad of about nineteen with a round, open, honest face, a button nose, friendly pale-blue eyes, a wide, warm grin and short, tight strawberry-blond curls. He wears a floppy, wide-brimmed dove-grey felt hat with a broad scarlet band, a loose white smock-shirt tied at the neck, a short oatmeal jerkin, moss-brown trousers tucked into thick ankle socks, and sturdy wooden clogs.

Rike-Per Kremmer rike-per-kremmer · Rich Per

En rik og sta kremmer som vil kontrollere datterens framtid og prøver å lure unna spådommen, men blir til slutt offer for sin egen grådighet.

A tall, bony man of about sixty with a long, horsey face, a jutting chin, a sharp hooked nose, small, darting, greedy grey eyes, a thin mouth, bushy salt-and-pepper side-whiskers and slicked-back black hair streaked with grey, with a sharp widow's peak. He wears a long wine-red wool coat with big bulging pockets, a green-and-gold striped silk waistcoat, grey knee breeches, white stockings and buckled shoes, gold rings on his fingers and a fat leather purse on his belt.

Per sin datter pers-datter · Per's Daughter

Den rike kremmerdatteren som blir gift med møllergutten gjennom et lurt brevbytte og får et nytt liv borte fra farens kontroll.

A tall, willowy woman in her mid-thirties with a long neck, a narrow face with a delicate chin, a small straight nose, soft brown eyes under pale brows, pink cheeks and a calm, patient expression. Her thick auburn hair hangs in one long plait to her waist, tied with a white ribbon. She wears a midnight-blue wool dress with a band of red-and-white woven trim at the hem and cuffs, and a round silver brooch at her collar.

Prinsessa hos Dragen prinsessa · the Princess

En bortført prinsesse som hjelper møllergutten med råd og styrke, og som blir reddet når Dragen blir drept.

A small, quick-witted young woman of about twenty-four with a round face, a pointed little chin, a small straight nose, bright dark eyes that miss nothing and a wry, lopsided smile. Her dark-brown hair is cut short in a cap of springy curls, held back by a thin silver band set with one pearl. She wears a long turquoise wool gown with wide bell sleeves, a silver-embroidered belt and soft grey slippers.

Dragen av Dybenfart dragen · the Dragon

Den farlige Dragen som bor i et svart slott ved den brede elva. Han vokter store skatter og har tre fjær i stjerten, og den som har dem, kan få hva han vil.

An ancient, heavy, pot-bellied dragon about twice as tall as a man, who walks upright on short, thick hind legs with big blunt claws. He has bumpy plum-purple scales dulled with age, a pale lavender belly, small leathery wings far too small for him, a long snout with round nostrils trailing grey smoke, big heavy-lidded amber eyes and a row of rust-orange spikes down his back. His long tail ends in exactly three long, shining golden feathers.

Ferjemannen ferjemannen · the Ferryman

En gammel mann bundet til å frakte folk over elva til Dragen, og som til slutt får avløsning ved å lure Rike-Per til å ta plassen hans.

A small, wiry, very old man, bent almost double with a back as crooked as a fish hook, yet strong as an ox. He has a wrinkled nut-brown face, a sharp beak of a nose, bright little black eyes under bushy snow-white eyebrows, a toothless grin, no beard, and thin white hair tied at the back in a stubby pigtail. He wears a battered wide-brimmed straw hat, a faded sea-green smock with patched elbows and grey trousers rolled up above the knee, and goes barefoot.

Han fylte pungen og reiste til stjernekikkerne. De så på stjernene og sa at det kunne de ikke se. Per ba dem se bedre etter. Han skulle betale godt. Da så de bedre etter, og da så de det: Dattera hans skulle få møllerbarnet som nettopp var kommet til verden i kverna rett nedenfor gården hans.

Per ba stjernekikkerne se bedre etter. Han skulle betale godt.

Alt: Tre gamle stjernekikkere står ved en stor messingkikkert på et tårntak en stjerneklar natt. Rike-Per står ved siden av og holder fram en tjukk pengepung.

english · after paragraph 5
So he took plenty of money with him to the stargazers and asked them to read in the stars what husband his daughter would get. The stargazers looked and looked, and said they couldn’t see it. Per begged them to look again, and look properly. He would pay them well. So they looked more closely, and then they said that his daughter was to marry the miller’s child who had just been born in the mill below Rich Per’s own farm.

Per begged them to look again, and look properly. He would pay them well.

Alt: Three old stargazers stand at a big brass telescope on a tower roof on a starry night. Rich Per stands beside them, holding out a fat purse of money.

A clear, frosty night on the flat stone roof of an old tower, under a sky thick with stars and a thin crescent moon. Three old stargazers in long dark-blue robes and fur caps, one tall and bald, one small with a long white beard and one thin with spectacles, crowd around a big brass telescope, the small one squinting into it. Rich Per leans in beside them with an impatient, greedy face, holding out a fat leather purse bulging with coins. Dark, snowy hills lie below.

He wears a collarless undyed linen shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long scorched brown leather apron, dark-blue wool breeches, heavy black boots and a red kerchief knotted round his neck.
- the Devil: A short, pot-bellied devil no taller than a boy of ten, with shiny tomato-red skin, a round face with a button nose, big goggly amber eyes, pointy ears, a long, pointed black goatee and two big black ram's horns curling out of his forehead. Setting:
- the Smithy: The inside of a small, sooty log smithy with a low beamed ceiling: a brick forge with a hood and glowing coals, a big leather bellows beside it, a black anvil on a thick tree stump in the middle, hammers, tongs and horseshoes hanging on the dark log walls, a wooden water barrel, and in the corner a big, deep armchair of worn dark-red leather. Wide double doors open onto bright sunshine and the dusty road.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, when Our Lord and Saint Peter still walked the earth. The smithy is a squat, soot-blackened log building with a turf roof, a crooked stone chimney and wide double doors, beside a dusty country road through farmland. A gnarled old pear tree heavy with yellow pears grows against its sunny wall. Inside are a brick forge with a big leather bellows, an anvil on a stump, tools on the walls and, in the corner, a big, deep armchair of worn dark-red leather. The steel-wire purse is a small, round coin purse of woven silver-grey steel wire with a snap clasp. Far along the road, the way forks: one road climbs into white clouds to the tall white gate of Heaven; the other dips into a smoky, rocky gully to the gate of Hell, a tall, crooked, soot-black iron gate with nine big locks.

This story's season, light and colours: Blazing summer heat in a dusty farming valley: glaring white-gold afternoons, parched straw-yellow fields, an ochre dust road and ripe yellow pears among dusty leaves. Inside the smithy: soot-black and charcoal lit by ember-orange glow and showers of sparks. At the end, soft white cloud and pale gold light at the gate of Heaven, and a smoky plum-purple haze at the gate of Hell.

En tynn skreddersvenn med strykejernet i hånda, som smeden tar igjen ved veiskillet, og som skal prøve å slippe inn i himmelen.

A thin, narrow-shouldered young journeyman tailor of about nineteen with a narrow pale face, a long pointed nose, big anxious grey eyes and neat, slicked-down black hair with a straight side parting. He wears a snug plum-purple waistcoat with a row of tiny silver buttons over a white shirt, grey knee breeches, white stockings and black buckle shoes, with a yellow tape measure round his neck and a red pincushion on his wrist, and carries a heavy black pressing iron.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, when Our Lord and Saint Peter still walked the earth. The smithy is a squat, soot-blackened log building with a turf roof, a crooked stone chimney and wide double doors, beside a dusty country road through farmland. A gnarled old pear tree heavy with yellow pears grows against its sunny wall. Inside are a brick forge with a big leather bellows, an anvil on a stump, tools on the walls and, in the corner, a big, deep armchair of worn dark-red leather. The steel-wire purse is a small, round coin purse of woven silver-grey steel wire with a snap clasp. Far along the road, the way forks: one road climbs into white clouds to the tall white gate of Heaven; the other dips into a smoky, rocky gully to the gate of Hell, a tall, crooked, soot-black iron gate with nine big locks.

This story's season, light and colours: Blazing summer heat in a dusty farming valley: glaring white-gold afternoons, parched straw-yellow fields, an ochre dust road and ripe yellow pears among dusty leaves. Inside the smithy: soot-black and charcoal lit by ember-orange glow and showers of sparks. At the end, soft white cloud and pale gold light at the gate of Heaven, and a smoky plum-purple haze at the gate of Hell.

Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

The wishing ring is a heavy silver ring with one round blue stone; the ring left in its place is a slim gold band. Halvor's horse is a shaggy, bony dun horse. The magic boots are cracked old brown leather boots. Soria Moria is a castle of glittering golden towers far beyond forests and mountains.

Characters

Halvor halvor · Halvor

En stille og undervurdert gutt som blir modig og sterk når han må, og som aldri gir opp før han finner den han elsker.

A tall, lanky young man of about nineteen with a lazy slouch, a long face, a long straight nose, sleepy, half-closed hazel eyes, a slow lopsided smile and messy auburn hair falling over his forehead, his cheeks smudged with soot. He wears a ragged, soot-streaked grey wool shirt with holes at the elbows, baggy patched brown breeches held up with a length of rope, grey wool stockings and battered brown leather shoes.

Halvor i fine klær halvor-fine · Halvor in Fine Clothes

Halvor kledd så fint at han ser ut som en kongssønn, med ønskeringen fra den yngste prinsessa på fingeren.

A tall, lanky young man of about nineteen with a long face, a long straight nose, sleepy hazel eyes, a slow lopsided smile and messy auburn hair falling over his forehead, washed clean and dressed like a king's son: a knee-length royal-blue wool tunic embroidered with gold at the collar and cuffs, a wide lingonberry-red sash, a white linen shirt, dark-grey hose, soft brown leather boots and a short dark-blue cloak fastened with a silver clasp.

Den eldste prinsessa eldest-princess · the Eldest Princess

Den eldste av de tre prinsessene. Hun sitter ved rokken i det første slottet, der trollet med tre hoder bor.

A tall, stately princess of about twenty-four with warm golden-brown skin, a long oval face, a straight nose, calm dark-brown eyes, neat arched eyebrows and thick black hair coiled into two round buns over her ears. She wears a thin gold circlet, a long plum-purple wool gown with a high collar and long sleeves, and a crisp white linen apron.

Den mellomste prinsessa middle-princess · the Middle Princess

Den mellomste av de tre prinsessene, fanget hos trollet med seks hoder. Da hun blir reddet, blir hun så glad at hun ikke vet hvilket bein hun skal stå på.

A short, lively princess of about twenty-one with warm golden-brown skin, a round face with dimpled cheeks, a small button nose, merry black eyes and glossy black hair cut in a thick, chin-length bob with a straight fringe. She wears a thin gold circlet, a long saffron-yellow wool gown with full sleeves and a wide white sash, and a string of big white pearls.

Den yngste prinsessa youngest-princess · the Youngest Princess

Den vakreste av de tre søstrene Halvor redder, som gir ham ønskeringen og forbyr ham å nevne dem, og som tar ringen tilbake da han bryter løftet.

A graceful, slender young woman of about nineteen with warm golden-brown skin, a heart-shaped face, a small straight nose, large, bright dark-brown eyes with long lashes, a calm, steady gaze and long, straight, glossy black hair falling loose to her waist. She wears a thin gold circlet, a long red wool gown with a square neckline and wide bell sleeves edged with gold braid, and a tiny gold sun pendant on a fine chain.

Trollet med tre hoder three-headed-troll · the Three-Headed Troll

Trollet i det første slottet, som stikker alle tre hodene inn gjennom døra og kjenner lukt av kristen manns blod.

A big, pear-shaped troll about twice as tall as a man, with knobbly blue-grey skin like wet slate, long dangling arms and huge flat feet. He has exactly three heads side by side on his broad shoulders, each with a big round nose: the left head is sleepy, with droopy eyelids and a floppy faded-red nightcap; the middle head is grumpy, with one bushy black eyebrow; the right head is surprised, with round eyes and a tuft of white hair. He wears a patched brown leather jerkin tied with rope.

Trollet med seks hoder six-headed-troll · the Six-Headed Troll

Trollet i det andre slottet, som er så svært at han må vri seg sidelengs inn gjennom døra.

A huge, barrel-shaped troll about three times as tall as a man, with pale sandstone-yellow skin covered in brown freckles, warts and crusty patches of lichen, and shoulders so wide that he must turn sideways to get through doors. He has exactly six heads in one long row along his shoulders, each with a long pointed nose, small beady eyes and a stiff tuft of black hair. He wears a huge patchwork coat sewn from old sacks and goes barefoot.

Trollet med ni hoder nine-headed-troll · the Nine-Headed Troll

Det største og farligste trollet, som vokter det tredje slottet og er seigere å beseire enn de andre.

An enormous troll, the biggest of the three, about four times as tall as a man, with dark charcoal-grey skin, rough and lumpy like wet rock and streaked with moss, a round belly and thick, stumpy legs. He has exactly nine small, round heads on short, thick necks, spread in a wide fan above his shoulders, each with a potato nose, bushy white eyebrows and a wide, frog-like mouth. He wears a ragged sheepskin cloak and a belt of knotted rope.

Halvors mor mother · the Mother

Halvors gamle mor, som ikke tror at den fine herren kan være gutten hennes, før skinnet fra glørne faller på ansiktet hans.

A small, sturdy, quick-moving old woman of about sixty with a round chin, a wide mouth made for laughing, a little upturned nose, bright brown eyes and grey-streaked dark-brown hair tucked under a faded indigo headscarf knotted on top of her head. She wears a patched heather-purple wool dress with rolled-up sleeves, a faded green apron and wooden clogs.

Halvors far father · the Father

Halvors gamle far, en stille mann som bukker for den fremmede herren og ikke vet om sønnen hans er levende eller død.

A broad, slow-moving, heavy-set old man of about sixty-five with a big round face, ruddy cheeks, a bulbous nose, a bushy salt-and-pepper beard and a bald head under a knitted blue cap. He wears a worn moss-green wool jacket over a collarless linen shirt, patched brown knee breeches, grey knitted stockings and heavy leather boots.

Kona med den lange nesa old-cottage-woman · the Old Woman

En gammel og underlig kvinne som hjelper Halvor videre ved å bytte bort støvler som gir enorme skritt og ved å spørre vestavinden om veien.

A tall, bony, very old woman with a long thin neck, knobbly hands, a wrinkled, cheerful face, small twinkling black eyes and an enormously long, thin, pointed nose with a rosy tip, long enough to poke the embers with. Wisps of dove-grey hair peep out from under a white linen cap. She wears a faded heather-blue wool dress, a black apron and wooden clogs.

Vestavinden west-wind · the West Wind

En kraftig og rastløs naturkraft som kjenner veien til Soria Moria og drar Halvor i vill fart over landet.

A wild, friendly wind spirit the size of a big man, with a round, rosy, beardless face, a wide merry grin and bright green eyes. His long streaming hair is made of whirling leaves and spruce needles, with three wooden clothes-pegs clipped in it. From the chest down his body turns into long, curling swirls of misty grey-green air full of spinning leaves, and he has long, thin, gusty arms.

Da han hadde gått et stykke, fant han en ring av vridde kvister, en sånn som folk brukte til å binde med. Den tok han med seg. Litt lenger borte fant han et skår av en skål. english · after paragraph 2
A little way along the road he found a willow withy, a ring of twisted willow for tying things with, and he picked it up. His patched sack hangs open from his shoulder, showing a ring of twisted willow, a shard of a blue-and-white bowl, two crooked goat horns and the black-and-white tail feathers of a magpie. He wears a patched rust-orange wool jacket with bone buttons over an undyed linen shirt, dark-green knee breeches, grey wool stockings, sturdy black leather boots and a small brown leather knapsack on his back.
