Story world: Old rural Norway at midsummer. The poor family lives in a tumbledown turf-roofed hut in a spruce forest. The royal farm lies in a green valley: log buildings stained ox-blood red, with turf roofs, carved gables, broad front steps and a long stable. The seven colts are glossy chestnut colts with flaxen manes and tails; the youngest and smallest has a white star on his forehead. As princes they are seven brothers from about twelve to twenty-two, with their sister's strawberry-blonde hair and shining white-and-gold clothes. The hag sits in a shallow cleft at the foot of a grey cliff beside a forest path. A huge white birch stump in a clearing hides the door to a small earthen room with a hearth, a great rusty sword and a little clay jar. Beyond a long wooden bridge over a river stands a small, dark, tarred church with a tall tower.

This story's season, light and colours: Midsummer: long, pale-gold days, a low sun that hardly sets and bright, pale nights under a lilac sky; violet mountains, purple heather, birch woods and dewy grass, with long golden shadows in the evenings. The wedding glows with warm candlelight.

Characters

Askeladden askeladden · Askeladden

Yngstesønnen som alle undervurderer, men som holder hodet kaldt, sier fra til kjerringa, og følger føllene helt til han finner sannheten og bryter forbannelsen.

A sturdy, broad-shouldered young man of about eighteen with full, round, sun-browned cheeks, a short straight nose, calm green eyes, a steady, determined smile and thick sandy-brown hair tied at the back of his neck with a leather cord. He wears a patched rust-orange wool jacket with bone buttons over an undyed linen shirt, dark-green knee breeches, grey wool stockings, sturdy black leather boots and a small brown leather knapsack on his back.

Kongen kongen · the King

Streng og mistenksom herre som setter en brutal prøve, men belønner den som faktisk klarer oppgaven.

A lean, severe king of about sixty, tall and straight-backed, with a long, bony face, stern frown lines, sharp, narrow hazel eyes under bushy black eyebrows and a short, neatly trimmed grey beard. He wears a long dark-red wool robe with a grey fur collar, a thick gold chain across his chest, a small, spiky gold crown and pointed black shoes.

Den gamle kjerringa i bergsprekken kjerringa-i-bergsprekken · the Spinning Hag

Listig gammel kone som lokker gjetere til å sløse bort dagen og gir dem falske svar til kongen.

A tiny, hunched old woman no taller than a ten-year-old child, with a small, wrinkled face, a very long, pointed nose that nearly touches her chin, little twinkling black eyes, a sweet, sly smile and wisps of white hair. She is wrapped in many layered shawls of faded blue, brown, plum and grey over a long dark skirt, wears worn felt slippers and always holds a distaff wound with grey wool.

Det yngste føllet (forhekset prins) det-yngste-follet · the Youngest Colt

Føllet som snakker med Askeladden og leder ham til stubben og kirken, der de får brød og vin som bevis på hva de spiser og drikker.

A small, slender chestnut colt, the youngest and smallest of seven, with long, knobbly legs, a glossy red-brown coat, a short flaxen mane that stands up like a brush, a long flaxen tail, soft pointed ears, big dark, clever eyes with long lashes and a neat white star on his forehead.

Den yngste prinsen den-yngste-prinsen · the Youngest Prince

Det yngste føllet slik han egentlig er: den yngste av de sju kongssønnene og lillebror til prinsessa.

A slight boy prince of about twelve, the youngest of seven brothers, with a round, freckled face, big dark eyes, a huge beaming smile and tousled strawberry-blonde hair. He wears shining white-and-gold clothes: a white tunic embroidered with gold, with a small white star on the chest, a short white cloak with gold trim, white hose and soft white leather boots.

Prinsessa prinsessa · the Princess

Kongens datter som blir Askeladdens brud, og som får se brødrene sine komme tilbake som prinser når forbannelsen brytes.

A cheerful princess of about nineteen with a round, freckled face, warm brown eyes, a wide, happy smile and a mass of bouncy strawberry-blonde curls falling past her shoulders, crowned with a small gold circlet set with one green stone. She wears a long pale-green wool gown with a white linen collar and cuffs, a gold-embroidered belt and soft green shoes.

Den eldste broren eldste-bror · the Eldest Brother

Askeladdens eldste bror, som drar ut for å tjene penger, men blir liggende hele dagen med hodet i fanget til kjerringa i bergsprekken.

A tall, gawky young man of about twenty-two with a long, bony face, a big chin, heavy-lidded eyes, a long nose, a lazy, lopsided grin and thick, wavy dark-blond hair that sticks up at the back. He wears a red-and-white checked homespun shirt with rolled sleeves, baggy brown breeches held up by a single strap and a wide, frayed straw hat, and he goes barefoot.

simplified · after paragraph 19
I grålysningen slapp stallmesteren ut føllene, og de fór av sted over berg og dal, med gutten etter. Og det gikk ham akkurat som broren. #08 · askeladden, det-yngste-follet
simplified · after paragraph 55
«Ja, nå må du ta sverdet med deg», sa føllet. «Med det skal du hogge hodet av oss alle sju på bryllupsdagen din. Da blir vi prinser igjen, slik vi var før. For vi er brødrene til prinsessa du skal få når du kan si kongen hva vi spiser og drikker. Men et fælt troll har forvandlet oss til føll. Når du har hogd hodene av oss, må du passe godt på å legge hvert hode ved halen på den kroppen det satt på. Da har trolldommen ikke makt over oss lenger.»

«Vi er brødrene til prinsessa du skal få.»

Alt: I det lille rommet under stubben holder Askeladden det store, rustne sverdet lett i den ene hånda og ei krukke i den andre. I døra står det yngste føllet og forteller ham hemmeligheten.

english · after paragraph 52
“Now you must take the sword with you,” said the colt. “With it you shall cut off the heads of all seven of us on your wedding day, and then we’ll be princes again, as we were before. For we are the brothers of the princess you shall have when you can tell the King what we eat and drink. But a wicked troll has put a spell on us. When you’ve cut off our heads, you must take great care to lay each head by the tail of the body it belonged to. Then the troll’s spell will have no more power over us.”

“We are the brothers of the princess you shall have.”

Alt: In the little room under the stump, Ash-Lad holds the great rusty sword lightly in one hand and a little jar in the other. In the doorway, the youngest colt tells him the secret.

Da føllene kom inn på kirkegården, ble de til mennesker igjen. De så ut som kongssønner, og klærne deres var så fine at det lyste av dem. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Young King: A stocky, wide-shouldered young king of about twenty-one with a frank, square face, a bumpy nose, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble along his jaw. He wears a small, plain gold crown with five points and a long white wool cloak bordered with silver embroidery of little waves over a chunky cream cabled sweater, dark-blue breeches and knee-high boots of tan leather.

Characters

Fiskergutten som blir konge gutten · the Fisher Lad

En modig og utholdende gutt oppdratt ved slottet, som kaster seg ut i prøvelser for å redde prinsessene og senere reiser verden rundt for å vinne dronningen tilbake.

A stocky, wide-shouldered young man of about twenty with a frank, square face, a bumpy nose, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble along his jaw. He wears a chunky, cream-coloured hand-knitted wool sweater with a cabled pattern, dark-blue homespun breeches and knee-high boots of tan leather, and a red handkerchief with white spots pokes out of his pocket.

Den unge kongen den-unge-kongen · the Young King

Fiskergutten når han har fått den yngste prinsessen til dronning. Han bryter løftet sitt og må lete i hele verden etter veien tilbake til Hvittenland.

A stocky, wide-shouldered young king of about twenty-one with a frank, square face, a bumpy nose, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble along his jaw. He wears a small, plain gold crown with five points and a long white wool cloak bordered with silver embroidery of little waves over a chunky cream cabled sweater, dark-blue breeches and knee-high boots of tan leather.

Fiskeren fiskeren · the Fisherman

Guttens far, som fisker til kongens bord og lover bort det han ikke vet at konen bærer på.

A lean, wiry fisherman of about forty-five with a long, weather-beaten face, deep laughter lines, a sharp nose, kind, crinkly blue eyes and a long, drooping black moustache but no beard. He wears a round, brimless sealskin cap, a thick grey wool jumper under a long, stiff apron of dark oiled leather, grey breeches tucked into heavy wooden-soled boots, and a coil of fishing line at his belt.

Den yngste prinsessen (dronningen av Hvittenland) den-yngste-prinsessen · the Youngest Princess

Den klokeste av de tre prinsessene, som vet hvordan trollene kan overvinnes, gir ham råd og en ring med to ønsker, og blir først borte når han bryter løftet.

A calm, thoughtful princess of about nineteen with a softly rounded chin, a small nose with a slight upturn, sea-grey eyes under soft brows, a quiet, knowing half-smile and long, wavy golden hair that flows down to her waist. A thin silver circlet with one pearl rests on her brow. She wears a plain sky-blue wool dress with long, close-fitting sleeves, a narrow belt of silver links and a hem sewn with small silver stars.

Dronningen av Hvittenland dronningen · the Queen

Den yngste prinsessen som dronning. Hun gir den unge kongen en ønskering, men må reise hjem igjen når han bryter løftet sitt.

A calm young queen of about nineteen with a softly rounded chin, a small nose with a slight upturn, sea-grey eyes under soft brows, a quiet, knowing half-smile and long, wavy golden hair that flows down to her waist. She wears a tall gold crown set with pale-blue stones, a sky-blue gown with a bodice laced with silver cord and a long train, and a short white fur cape fastened with a round silver clasp.

Det ni-hodede trollet trollet-med-ni-hoder · the Nine-Headed Troll

Den farligste av trollene som holder prinsessene fanget, pisker gutten til han besvimer og prøver å knuse ham, men blir til slutt hugget ned.

An enormous troll that fills a room up to the ceiling, with a huge, round, lumpy body of pale, chalky-cream hide blotched with big peat-brown patches like an old birch stump, stumpy legs and big round hands. Nine heads grow in a ring around the top of its body like a crown of boulders, each with a broad pinkish snout, small sleepy brown eyes, floppy ears and a wide mouth. It wears a huge, ragged smock of faded red-and-white checked homespun.

Nordavinden nordavinden · the North Wind

En mektig, personifisert vind som hjelper den unge kongen ved å skape storm ved slottet og blåse rivalen bort.

A tall, lean, long-limbed storm giant, three times as tall as a man, with a long, bony, windburnt face, hollow cheeks, a long thin nose, a wide mouth pursed to blow and bright, shining silver eyes. His wild, tangled slate-grey hair and long, wispy beard stream sideways as if in a gale. He wears a huge, billowing cloak made of dark-grey storm clouds, torn into ragged wisps at the edges, and from the knees down he fades into swirling grey mist.

english · after paragraph 51
The third brother blew his horn, and all the fish in the sea came swimming until the water boiled with them. But none of them knew a thing. At last there came an old, old pike. She was so slow and heavy that he had to blow and blow before she arrived. When the king asked her, she said:

Alt: At the edge of a cold grey sea, the water boils with fish, and a huge old pike rises among them. The young king kneels on a rock, leaning towards her.

Alt: A young woman with raven-black hair stands in a bog white with bog-cotton, her arms full. Above her, twelve wild ducks fly past in the sunrise.

Sunrise on the White Bog, the first low light catching every tuft of bog cotton. The Maiden stands knee-deep among the white tufts with her arms full of bog cotton and her lips pressed together in silence, and looks up as twelve wild ducks fly low over her head in a long line against the pale-gold sky. A full sack rests on a tussock beside her.

The Maiden stands knee-deep among the white tufts with her arms full of bog cotton and her lips pressed together in silence, and looks up as twelve wild ducks fly low over her head in a long line against the pale-gold sky. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Maiden: A slender young woman of about twenty with snow-pale skin, rosy-red cheeks and lips, a soft oval face, a small straight nose and large dark-grey eyes with long black lashes. Her raven-black hair hangs in one thick, loose braid over her shoulder, tied with a strip of white linen. She wears a plain dark-teal homespun wool dress with a deep pocket, where the handle of a small silver spoon peeks out, a long grey wool shawl and thin, worn brown leather shoes.

Setting:
- the White Bog: A vast, flat forest bog stretching as far as the eye can see, so thick with nodding white tufts of bog cotton that it looks covered in snow, with dark pools of water, reeds, tussocks of moss and heather, and a few stunted pines. A low ridge with dark spruce forest rims the far side, where the sun comes up.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The royal manors are clusters of dark log buildings with turf roofs, carved gables and small leaded windows around a yard. The Queen's sleigh is small and red, drawn by two brown horses. The thirteen silver spoons are small and exactly alike. As wild ducks, the twelve brothers are mallard drakes with glossy bottle-green heads, white neck rings, chestnut breasts and grey backs. As men they look alike: pale, with tousled raven-black hair, bottle-green caps and chestnut-brown tunics; the eldest is the tallest and has a short black beard. Bog cotton grows in fluffy white tufts, and the caps, shirts and kerchiefs sewn from it are pure white. The snake pit is an old, dank walled stone yard behind the young King's manor. The three children are two small boys with fair curls and a baby girl with black hair.

This story's season, light and colours: One long tale through many seasons: a hushed white winter day of fresh snow under a low, pale sun at the start; mossy spruce-green forest and warm firelight in the brothers' cabin; the bog at sunrise, a sea of white bog cotton in thin mist and pale-gold light; cool grey stone and candlelight at the young King's manor; a smoky orange pyre glow under a slate-blue dusk; and a clear, fresh spring morning at the end. Accents of pure white, blood red and raven black.

Snøhvit og Rosenrød som dronning snohvit-og-rosenrod-dronning · the Maiden Queen

Snøhvit og Rosenrød etter at hun har giftet seg med den unge kongen. Hun syr på skjortene hver dag og kan ikke si et ord, selv når den gamle dronningen lyver om henne.

A slender young queen of about twenty-four with snow-pale skin, rosy-red cheeks and lips, a soft oval face, a small straight nose and large dark-grey eyes with long black lashes. Her raven-black hair hangs in one thick, loose braid over her shoulder under a slender silver circlet. She wears a long, plain gown of white linen embroidered with small red roses at the hem and cuffs, a deep-red girdle and soft grey leather slippers.

Dronningen dronningen · the Queen

Moren til de tolv prinsene og Snøhvit og Rosenrød. Hun ønsket seg en datter så hvit som snø og så rød som blod, og måtte gi bort sønnene sine for å få henne.

A warm, motherly queen of about forty-five with a round face, a soft double chin, a small snub nose, kind hazel eyes, rosy cheeks and wavy chestnut hair going grey at the temples, pinned up under a small gold crown. She wears a long plum-purple wool cloak lined and trimmed with thick white fur over a plum gown, white fur mittens and fur-lined boots.

Trollkjerringa trollkjerringa · the Troll Hag

Ei trollkjerring som dukker opp i snøen og lover dronningen en datter, men som vil ha de tolv sønnene hennes i bytte.

A short, stout old troll woman, no taller than a fence rail, with lumpy, sandy-beige skin like weathered sandstone, a huge knobbly nose shaped like a big potato, small beady black eyes, a wide crooked grin with three teeth and an enormous tangle of black-and-grey hair like a crow's nest, stuck with twigs and one black feather. A thin cow's tail with a tuft pokes out under her patched grey skirt, and she wears a ragged moss-green shawl and big grey felt boots.

Den unge kongen den-unge-kongen · the Young King

Landets konge som finner henne på myra, gifter seg med henne, og som til slutt forstår sannheten når brødrene hennes kommer tilbake.

A tall, slim young king of about twenty-six, clean-shaven, with a long, friendly face, a straight nose, warm brown eyes, a wide smile and fair, straight hair tied back at the neck with a dark-blue ribbon, a thin gold circlet on his head. He wears a sky-blue wool coat trimmed with white braid, a broad brown leather belt, fawn breeches, soft grey leather boots and a short grey riding cloak.

Kongens stemor (den gamle dronningen) kongens-stemor · the Stepmother

Misunnelig og hensynsløs, stjeler dronningens barn og legger skylden på henne for å få henne dømt til døden.

A bony, very upright old dowager queen with a long, pointed chin, a small hooked nose, narrow darting black eyes, thin lips and a chalk-pale face with two hard spots of rouge. Her steel-grey hair is piled high in a tall coil stuck with jewelled pins. She wears a stiff black wool gown shot with silver thread, a high collar of grey lace, rings on every finger and a small silver hand mirror on a chain at her waist.

Den yngste broren den-yngste-broren · the Youngest Brother

Den yngste av de tolv brødrene, som er villender om dagen og prinser om natta. Han forsvarer søsteren sin da den eldste vil drepe henne.

A slim young man of about twenty-three, the smallest of twelve brothers, with snow-pale skin, a narrow, gentle face, a small straight nose, large dark-grey eyes and tousled raven-black hair that sticks up at the back like ruffled feathers. He wears a faded bottle-green wool cap, a worn chestnut-brown wool tunic with a white linen collar and a rope belt, patched grey breeches and soft grey leather boots.

Den yngste broren med andevingen den-yngste-broren-vinge · the Winged Brother

Den yngste broren når trolldommen er brutt. Skjorta hans fikk aldri venstre erme, så han har en andevinge der han skulle hatt venstre arm.

A slim young man of about twenty-six with snow-pale skin, a narrow, gentle face, a small straight nose, large dark-grey eyes and tousled raven-black hair that sticks up at the back like ruffled feathers. He wears a new pure-white cap, shirt and kerchief of soft bog-cotton cloth, grey breeches and soft grey leather boots. In place of his left arm he has a large wild duck's wing of grey-brown feathers with a shiny blue-violet patch edged in white.

- the Troll Hag: A short, stout old troll woman, no taller than a fence rail, with lumpy, sandy-beige skin like weathered sandstone, a huge knobbly nose shaped like a big potato, small beady black eyes, a wide crooked grin with three teeth and an enormous tangle of black-and-grey hair like a crow's nest, stuck with twigs and one black feather. A thin cow's tail with a tuft pokes out under her patched grey skirt, and she wears a ragged moss-green shawl and big grey felt boots.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The royal manors are clusters of dark log buildings with turf roofs, carved gables and small leaded windows around a yard. The Queen's sleigh is small and red, drawn by two brown horses. The thirteen silver spoons are small and exactly alike. As wild ducks, the twelve brothers are mallard drakes with glossy bottle-green heads, white neck rings, chestnut breasts and grey backs. As men they look alike: pale, with tousled raven-black hair, bottle-green caps and chestnut-brown tunics; the eldest is the tallest and has a short black beard. Bog cotton grows in fluffy white tufts, and the caps, shirts and kerchiefs sewn from it are pure white. The snake pit is an old, dank walled stone yard behind the young King's manor. The three children are two small boys with fair curls and a baby girl with black hair.

This story's season, light and colours: One long tale through many seasons: a hushed white winter day of fresh snow under a low, pale sun at the start; mossy spruce-green forest and warm firelight in the brothers' cabin; the bog at sunrise, a sea of white bog cotton in thin mist and pale-gold light; cool grey stone and candlelight at the young King's manor; a smoky orange pyre glow under a slate-blue dusk; and a clear, fresh spring morning at the end. Accents of pure white, blood red and raven black.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.

Fra den dagen hadde prinsessa ingen ro på seg. Hun ville av sted, og hun måtte av sted, for å lete etter brødrene sine. Alt sammen var jo hennes skyld, syntes hun. Picture: Night in the candlelit Little Chamber, rain streaking the small window. The Girl sits at the spinning wheel with a hopeless tangle of pale-gold flax in her lap and looks up in surprise: the door has creaked open, and three old faces peer round it, one above the other: the Long-Nosed Aunt at the top with her enormous nose poking far into the room, the Teary-Eyed Aunt in the middle dabbing her huge eyes, and the Broad-Hipped Aunt at the bottom, her wide striped skirt filling the doorway.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Girl: A slim, cheerful hunter's daughter of about eighteen with an oval face dusted all over with freckles, a snub nose, big hazel eyes, a wide smile and mousy-brown hair in one thick plait over her shoulder. She wears a plain pine-green linen dress with the sleeves rolled up, a short brown sheepskin vest, a leather belt and sturdy brown shoes, and has a blue jay feather tucked behind one ear.
- the Long-Nosed Aunt: A small, slim, spry old woman of about eighty who holds herself very upright, with a kindly, wrinkled face, merry little blue eyes, rosy cheeks and crooked, work-worn hands. Her nose is enormous: thick as a cucumber at the root and nearly six feet long, it sticks straight out in front of her like a branch and ends in a round pink tip. Her white hair is in a small knot. She wears a long nut-brown dress and a big moss-green fringed shawl, and leans on a crooked walking stick.
- the Teary-Eyed Aunt: A round-shouldered old woman of about eighty, of middle height, with a soft, wrinkled face and enormous round eyes as big as small plates, red-rimmed and always running with tears, so she keeps dabbing them with a big white lace handkerchief. Her silver hair is braided and pinned in a ring on top of her head. She wears a dusty-rose dress with a white collar, a red tomato-shaped pincushion on her wrist and a silver thimble on one finger.
- the Broad-Hipped Aunt: A short old woman of about eighty with narrow shoulders, a small round head and enormously broad hips and backside, so wide that she can only just squeeze through a door and her skirt looks like a haystack. She has a square little face, a snub nose, bright squinting eyes, a gap-toothed grin and grey hair in a tight bun under a small round black felt hat. She wears a huge, bell-shaped skirt with wide red and ochre stripes, a white blouse and a short dark-brown knitted jacket.

- the Little Chamber: A small room of its own up under the roof of the royal manor, with dark log walls and a low, beamed ceiling. A narrow wooden bed with a woollen blanket stands against one wall, a small table and a candlestick sit under a four-paned leaded window with rain running down the glass, a wooden spinning wheel stands beside it, a big upright wooden loom fills the far corner, and a plank door has an iron latch.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The royal manor is a big cluster of dark log buildings with turf roofs, carved gables and small leaded windows around a cobbled yard. The flax is soft, pale-gold fibre in a great heap; spun, it becomes smooth, shining pale-gold thread wound in coils; woven, it becomes a thick bolt of fine cream-white linen; sewn, it becomes a pile of white linen shirts with buttons. The Queen's other maids are three young women in grey wool dresses, white aprons and white linen caps. The wedding feast is held in the Great Hall, with a long table, candles and six guests in festive clothes.

Accents: flax gold and the Queen's rainbow-striped knitting.

En sta og smart gåsepike som vet hva hun vil, og som til slutt avsløres som den rette for prinsen.

A small, sturdy young woman of about eighteen, a head shorter than most, with a round, sun-browned face, a small determined chin, a snub nose, calm dark-brown eyes that look straight at you and thick, straight eyebrows. Her thick dark-brown hair is in one short, stubby plait tied with red wool. She wears a plain brown wool dress mended with patch on patch of blue and green, a white apron, wooden clogs and a little patchwork sewing bag at her waist.

Kongssønnen fra England kongssonnen · the Prince

En prins som leter etter en brud og bruker en magisk stein for å finne sannheten.

A tall, lean prince of about twenty-four with a long, kind face, a slightly long straight nose, calm hazel eyes, neat sandy hair parted at the side and a small, neatly trimmed sandy moustache, with a polite, patient smile. He wears a thin gold circlet, a scarlet wool tunic with gold braid across the chest, a long scarlet riding cloak, cream hose and brown riding boots with turned-down cuffs.

Sannhetssteinen sannhetssteinen · the Knowing Stone

En magisk stein som avslører hvem som er ren og hvem som lyver når noen går over den.

A small, smooth, egg-shaped stone no bigger than a plum, polished like a river pebble, milky white with faint swirls of pale gold and rose inside. It has no face and never moves, but when it speaks, or someone steps over it, it glows with a soft, warm golden light that spreads around it like candlelight.

Den tredje prinsessen tredje-prinsesse · the Third Princess

Den siste av prinsessene som prøver å lure prinsen ved å sende Aase i stedet for seg.

A tall, willowy princess of about twenty with a long neck, a narrow face, high arched brows over big, anxious dark-brown eyes, a delicate little mouth and glossy chocolate-brown hair in long, bouncy ringlets tied back with a pearl-studded ribbon. She wears a thin circlet of pearls, pearl earrings and a long peacock-blue gown with full sleeves and a lace collar, and carries a white feather fan that she likes to hide behind.
